abstract: We have developed a near-field spectrometer operating in the THz-range between 30 GHz and 1.4 THz, where we use backward-wave oscillators (BWO) as continues wave sources and a photo-induced aperture as near-field probe. This instrument allows performing THz-imaging and spectroscopy with sub-wavelength resolution without a complicated probe-sample distance control and with a continuously adjustable aperture.

articleTitle: Application of Prony's Method to High Range Resolution radar
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: This paper applies the Prony's method to millimeter wave stepped frequency radar.

articleTitle: Atmospheric Observations by a Balloon-Borne Superconducting Submillimeter-Wave Limb-Emission Sounder
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A balloon-borne superconducting submillimeter-wave limb-emission sounder was developed to measure stratospheric molecules. It carries a 300 mm-diameter offset parabolic antenna, a 620-650 GHz heterodyne SIS receiver, and an acousto-optical spectrometer. T<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sys</sub>(DSB) is less than 460 K at 624-639 GHz with a best value of 330 K(11 hv/k<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</sub>). BSMILES was launched from Japan in 2003 and 2004. All systems operated properly and emission line spectra of O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, CIO, HO, HO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> etc. were measured. After the observations, the gondola splashed on the Pacific Ocean and was retrieved.

articleTitle: THz-wave generation and detection from ZnSe crystal induced by femtosecond laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We studied competing mechanism of terahertz (THz) generation in ZnSe surface irradiated by femtosecond laser pulses. We experimentally presented both transient current and optical rectification contributions to obtain THz radiation.

articleTitle: Study of the electron emission from PZT ferroelectric cathodes
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Electron emission from ferroelectrics is a new type of stimulated strong electron emission which is potential widely used as cold cathode. PZT ferroelectric grating cathodes is prepared by lithography technology. High voltage pulse was applied to the rear electrode, the ferroelectric ceramic polarization switch and electron emission from ferroelectric cathodes is observed. The effect of various experimental conditions on the characteristics and mechanism of strong electron emission from the ferroelectric cathodes is analyzed include ceramic polarity and the driving pulse shape. A feasible driving circuit is presented.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis On Input Cavity Of 8mm Gyroklystron
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Modulator cavity of multi-cavitys gyroklystron transforms the TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">411</sub> mode in out cavity to TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">011</sub> mode in inner resonant cavity through 4 slots, TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">011</sub> mode is used to modulate the transverse velocity of gyroelectron beam.In this paper , an analysis of cold cavity is presented , HFSS code is used to simulate couple of structure variety accurately and revise approximate analysis.lt shows ratio of inner cavity's energy storage to that of outer cavity's is 41.65, When angle between coupling slots' midline & waveguide axis is 45deg. Length of slots affects Q factor greatly while resonance frequency is insensitive to it,moreover,Q factor relate with length of slots more sensitive than width of them.Energy storage in coaxial cavity has been calculated.Based on a large number of calculations and simulations, the optimal modulator cavity meeting the design requirement is attained.

articleTitle: Actively Controlled Enhancement Cavity For Terahertz Generation
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We report on the efficient Cherenkov-type terahertz (THz) generation using lithium niobate crystals and a high repetition rate femtosecond laser. An actively length controlled synchronously pumped ring resonator acts as an enhancement cavity for the near infrared pump and therefore recycles the available pump power towards a higher terahertz output. A seven times higher THz field amplitude was measured with electro-optical sampling.

articleTitle: Single-Polarization Single-Mode Photonic Crystal Fiber for Terahertz Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A new type of highly birefringent polyethylene rectangular lattice photonic crystal fiber (RLPCF) was investigated. This PCF can operate at single-polarization single-mode (SPSM). By changing the structure parameters of the RLPCF, the mode index of the two linearly polarized principal states can be designed. Results show that the PCF has higher birefringence than regular RLPCF. Furthermore, the polyethylene material that is transparent to terahertz wave is inexpensive and easy to operate. This PCF is an effective component for some THz systems.

articleTitle: Enhanced transmission in photonic crystal of hole arrays
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A novel electromagnetic band gap structure made of several stacked sub-wavelength hole arrays is presented. Simulation results show its potential in dichroic filters applications. A prototype operating in the millimeter wave frequency range has been fabricated and measured by means of a quasioptical vector network analyzer. The experimental results confirm the potential of these novel structures in order to obtain novel and surprising electromagnetic properties.

articleTitle: Terahertz detection and emission related to two dimensional plasma oscillations in nanometer size transistors
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In this work we present an overview of experimental results on THz detection and emission by nanotransistors. We present recent results on THz emission obtained in different types of InGaAs/InP and GaN/AlGaN nanometric high electron mobility transistors.

articleTitle: Terahertz absorption in spintronic superlattices
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In this work, we present a theoretical Investigation of optical absorption in a spintronic superlattice. It is shown that the Rashba spin-orbit interaction can be used to control the characteristics of the absorption. Our results suggest possible experiments to detect such tunable absorption spectra. The underlying mechanism is the level splitting and linear energy dispersion, both are the consequences of spin-orbit interaction. The proposed absorption properties can be useful in developing spintronic devices in the terahertz regime.

articleTitle: FADIS: Project for Fast Directional Switching of Discrete High Power Millimeter Wave Beams
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In tokamaks and stellarators, for combining discrete wave beams and switching the combined beams to different launchers or ports (for instance, to suppress hydrodynamic plasma instabilities), some versions of structures fed by phase-or narrow-band-frequency-controlled CW gyrotrons are proposed.

articleTitle: Rigorous Analysis of Multiport Waveguide Junctions with Diaphragms
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A rigorous electromagnetic analysis of a multiport H-plane waveguide junction with a diaphragm is presented.

articleTitle: A New Method for Constructing Electromagnetic Dyadic Green Functions in Two Kinds of Boundary Conditions
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Based on the method of vector eigenfunction expansion, using the mapping in one-dimensional space of the boundary conditions of vector wave functions, a new method for constructing electromagnetic dyadic Green functions in Dirichlet boundary conditions and Neumann boundary conditions is developed in this paper. The method is not related to specific configurations or coordinate systems, which makes it more applicable to arbitrary cylindrical structures.

articleTitle: Proposal of Resonant Tunneling Diode Oscillators with Offset-Fed Slot Antennas in THz and Sub-THz Range
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We propose resonant tunneling diode (RTD) oscillators with offset-fed slot antennas in THz and sub-THz range for high frequency and high output power oscillators at room temperature. We analyzed the dependence of the oscillation frequency and output power on RTD position along slot antenna using 3-dimensional electromagnetic-field simulation. The oscillation frequency and output power largely increase compared with previously reported oscillators without offset feed, because of improvement on impedance matching between RTD and antenna. The oscillation frequency of 100-mum-long slot antenna without offset is around 300 GHz, while it increases to around 1 THz by the offset of 46.5 mum (93%) from the antenna center.

articleTitle: Application of Amplified Femtosecond Ytterbium Fiber Laser for the THz Time-Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We report the application of a newly developed femtosecond fiber laser for the THz time-domain spectroscopy. Ytterbium doped fiber was used for generation of laser pulses at wavelength 1.06 mum with the further amplification. The use of novel SESAM (semiconductor saturable absorber mirror) device made it possible to get pulse duration less than 200 fs on the 3 average power up to 1 W at the 50 MHz pulse repetition rate. We analyze the nonlinear and semiconductor devices optimal for the generation and electro optical detection of THz pulses in the time-domain systems based on the femtosecond ytterbium fiber laser.

articleTitle: Omnidirectional Reflection of Light Waves On Si/SiO2 Multilayer Films
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We have investigated the reflection of electromagnetic waves on the Si/SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> multilayer films. The film is fabricated by magnetron sputtering technique. For all polarizations of incident light, reflectance measurements demonstrate a wide omnidirectional photonic band gap. The resonant modes within the photonic band gap are observed at the telecommunication wavelengths. The experimental results are in good agreement with numerical simulations. The feature of this type of film achieves the potential applications in wavelength division multiplexing devices.

articleTitle: Terahertz emission from various organic crystals
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We have measured terahertz emission from various organic crystals excited by femtosecond pulses. Our four emitters are 3,5-dimethyl-1-(4-nitrophyenyl)-1,2,4-triazole (DMNT), 3,9-dinitro-5a,6,11a,12-tetrahydro-[1,4]benzoxazino [3,2-b][1,4] benzoxazine (DNBB), 1-(2-thienyl)-3-(4-methyl-phenyl) propenone (TC-28), and 1-(3-thienyl)-3-(4-bromphenyl) propenone (TC-122). Bandwidths of these emitters are achieved to be more than 4 THz.

articleTitle: Shock Wave Generation by Millimeter-wave Plasma using a High Power Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A high power millimeter-wave beam generated by a 170 GHz gyrotron was injected into a cylindrical tube and atmospheric plasma was generated. The ionization front and a shock wave were propagated in the tube during the millimeter-wave pulse. From the pressure history measurement and plasma emission imaging in the tube, the propagation velocity of the shock wave was found identical to that of the ionization front. This indicates that isometric heating at the ionization front by millimeter-wave causes the efficient energy conversion from millimeter wave to fluid.

articleTitle: A 2D Electron Optics System Code for Millimeter Wave Traveling-Wave Tubes
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: To improve the performance of the electron optics system for millimeter wave traveling-wave tubes, we developed a two-dimensional electron optics system design tool. It includes UESTCGun, UESTCPPM and UESTCMDC to model and simulate electron guns, periodic permanent magnetic focusing systems and multi-stage depressed collectors respectively. The physics models and implements of UESTCGun code, UESTCPPM code and UESTCMDC code will be presented.

articleTitle: Cryogenic excitation and detection of terahertz radiation in microstrip circuits
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: There are widespread potential applications for guided-wave terahertz (THz) frequency measurements in the study of condensed matter physical systems, many of which require a low temperature environment. Here we report on the excitation, propagation and detection of ~picosecond duration (>1 THz bandwidth) electrical pulses at cryogenic temperatures (~4 K) in microstrip circuits. A reduction in both the excitation and propagating pulse widths is observed compared to room temperature data. These results indicate that, in cryogenic THz circuits, the electrical properties of low-temperature-grown GaAs are highly suited to photoconductive excitation and detection, and that benzocyclobutene (BCB) acts an effective THz dielectric material.

articleTitle: The Analysis of Ion Noise With Beam-Wave Interaction in Klystron by Two dimension Particle Simulation Method
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Ion noise in output signal in klystron was obtained by particle in cell method. The phase fluctuation in output signal is caused by the change of the beam current DC velocity which is affected by the change of the ion amount. The phase of output signal changed with the change of beam electron amount.

articleTitle: Application of Surface Antireflection Treating in Infrared Thermal Wave Nondestructive Testing
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The application of surface antireflection technique in infrared thermal wave nondestructive testing is presented. The method for covering antireflection membrane on the specimen surface by vacuum-pumping has been tested. The experimental results show that this technique is effective for enhancing sample surface absorption and emissivity, moreover, it does not stain or damage the specimen.

articleTitle: Wide-Band Heterodyne-Radiometer with Fast Frequency-Switching Local Oscillator for Electron Cyclotron Emission Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In the report, a backward wave oscillator (-100 GHz) was used as a local oscillator. In this work, a fast-switching local oscillator part in lower frequency range was built for higher time resolution. The lower frequency becomes wide-band in millimeter-wave range (-100 GHz) using millimeter multipliers. The local-frequency part plays an important role to determine the frequency switching-time, step-width and total range in the ECE measuremt. The frequency switching of the lower local-frequency part is mainly discussed in this report.

articleTitle: Gyrotron Radiation Affected by Modulated Reflector: High Power Experiment
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A special experiment performed at the TJ-II stellarator set-up has demonstrated how a relatively weak wave returned from an external mechanically modulated reflector influences upon the gyrotron radiation spectrum.

articleTitle: Study of the Field Characteristics in Helical Wave-guide
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The mode coupling rules, dispersion characteristics and field distribution of wave-guide with introduction helical corrugation are analyzed using traveling wave theory. According to the simulation results characteristics of operating mode are illuminated.

articleTitle: Carrier Transport in type-II Mid-IR Interband Cascade Laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Two efficient depopulation processes in type-II interband cascade laser: LO-phonon assisted hole transition between hole wells and interband tunneling between the hole well and InAs well, are investigated.

articleTitle: Terahertz Gas Laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: CS<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser with optical pumping has been offered for obtaining powerful T-rays. As a pumping source CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser oscillating on the hot band (wavelength 11.4 mum) has been used. Calculations have shown that at the optimal conditions the output 0.1 J at the peak power 1 MW can be obtained. The spectral tuning (2-3 THz) over the ro-vibrational lines is possible.

articleTitle: Composite High-Q Micrsostrip Resonator Using Effective Highly Dispersive Materials
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A composite high-Q miicrostrip resonator is proposed by using effective highly dispersive (EHD) materials with electromagnectically-induced-transparency-like (EIT-like) spectrum. We show that a defective microstrip photonic crystal (PC) can be utilized as an EIT-like material with dispersion controlled by simply adjusting the structure parameters. Both simulation and experiment results demonstrate that, compared to traditional methods, Q-factor boosts much more quickly and peak-transmission decreases much slower at the same time for composite resonator.

articleTitle: True Time Delay Beam Steering/Shaping Phased Array Antenna System for Plasma Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: An electronically controlled beam focusing/ defocusing Phased Array Antenna (PAA) system is proposed for use in Microwave Imaging Reflectometry (MIR) systems, which are being developed to measure plasma density fluctuations. The design, construction and performance of a Ka-band 1times8 true time delay E-plane beam scanning and broadening phased array system based on piezoelectric transducer controlled delay line technology using antipodal elliptically-tapered slot antennas are presented. The beam is steered from -21degto +24degand the 3 dB beamwidth is widened by about 10deg, the latter being the requirement for the target MIR system.

articleTitle: Terahertz transmission spectroscopic analysis of mono- and di-substituted hydroxynaphthalenes in the 0.5- to 6- THz region using GaP THz wave generator
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We report the room temperature terahaertz (THz) transmission spectroscopy measurements of mono-and di-substituted hydroxynaphthalenes in the 0.5-to 6-THz region using a GaP THz wave generator. Several absorption peaks were observed and ascribed to be the fundamental vibrational modes of each of the isomers which were also validated by ab initio calculations. The absorption peak at 4 THz is attributed to the twisting of the 1,4-naphthol about its longer axis while the absorption peak at 5 THz is due to the butterfly motion of the naphthol about its shorter axis.

articleTitle: Dual-signal-wavelength Optical Parametric Generator Based on ppr-PP-MgO:LN
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A pulsed nanosecond optical parametric generator(OPG) in a periodically phased-reversed MgO-doped periodically poled lithium niobate(ppr-PP-MgO:LN) was demonstrated. Two pairs of signal waves and idler waves were obtained with a maximum output power of 135 mW repeating at a rate of 25 kHz.

articleTitle: THz Spectral Study Of MgF2:Co Crystals
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The THz spectra of MgF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and MgF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>:Co crystals have been measured by Time Domain THz Spectral technology. The optical parameters of the crystals have been calculated.

articleTitle: Demonstration of a 93-GHz Communication System Based on a High-Sensitivity SIS Receiver
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A millimeter-wave communication system incorporating with a 100-GHz superconducting SIS (superconductor-insulator-superconductor) receiver is demonstrated. The SIS receiver has an intermediate frequency (IF) band of 1.1-1.7 GHz and an equivalent input noise temperature less than 50 K, while the transmitter is a 93-GHz varactor-tunable Gunn oscillator with its output frequency modulated via an 11-MHz signal source. In addition, two analog FM demodulation techniques are adopted in this experiment.

articleTitle: Optical Properties of Ultra-thin Metal Films
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: While the optical properties as well as the DC-conductivity of thicker metal films are well understood, little has been done at and below the metal-to-insulator transition (percolation threshold), especially in the infrared and far-infrared region. Here we present temperature dependent FTIR measurements on ultra-thin Au films on Si(111 ) in the thickness range between about one monolayer and 9 nm.

articleTitle: Focusing by the two-dimension photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We investigate the square-lattice dielectric photonic crystals that have been used to demonstrate flat slab focusing experimentally by Parimi et al. Using the multiple scattering methods, we have demonstrated that the left-handed mode and the right-handed mode are excited simultaneously. After changing the radius of the alumina rods, the focusing properties of this photonic crystal slab are dominantly governed by the negative refraction effect because the left-handed mode is strongly enhanced while the right-handed mode is strongly suppressed.

articleTitle: Tunable quasi-monolithic THz-wave parametric oscillator in a ring-cavity configuration
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We demonstrated a continuously tunable quasi-monolithic THz-wave parametric oscillator. A 5 mol% MgO:LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> crystal within dimensions of 15 times 20 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> was used as a nonlinear optical crystal. Frequency-tunability of THz-wave radiation was obtained by moving the super mirror linearly. The tunable range from 1.65 to 2.71 THz was obtained, which was derived from measured idler wavelength and pump wavelength with an optical spectrum analyzer.

articleTitle: Mid-Infrared Tunable Diode Laser Absorption Spectroscopy for Gas Sensing
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Most of gaseous materials show characteristic optical absorptions, especially in the mid-infrared (2-25 mum) band. The optical fingerprints of different gases have made the spectral absorption a unique method of gas analysis. The tunable diode laser absorption spectroscopy (TDLAS) method use a compact single mode diode laser tuning over an interested wavelength range swiftly can fulfill the function of spectroscopy scan. In this talk the TDLAS experiments using home made mid-infrared diode lasers for gas sensing are represented, and various effects affecting the performance of the sensor have been discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis of Infrared Thermal Wave Nondestructive Testing On Flat Bottom Hole Sample by the Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The infrared thermal wave nondestructive testing(NDT) experiment is carried on to the flat bottom hole sample made of stainless steel, and the experimental process is simulated by the filnite element method. The simulation result compared with experiment can support the theoretical reference and further quality measurement of the infrared thermal wave NDT technique.

articleTitle: On Conditions of Long-Living Electron Bunch Excitation in Undulator
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Theoretical and experimental investigations of conditions of electron bunch excitation in undulator have been theoretically studied. The relation between bunch dimensions, number of electrons and bunch lifetime has been obtained by using the virial theorem. The spontaneous radiation of non-relativistic electron beam is experimentally shown in a system with axial symmetrical magnetic disks.

articleTitle: THz Emitters and Detectors Based on Ion Implanted III-V Semiconductors
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Ultrafast charge carrier dynamics in semiconducting materials ultimately determine the performance of photoconductive terahertz (THz) emitters and receivers. Ion implantation of III-V semiconductors allows carrier dynamics to be tailored for a particular application, and thus the technique is increasingly being applied to the development of advanced materials for terahertz photonics. In this talk I will briefly introduce the technique of ion implantation and review some recent applications in THz photonics. 1 will then present time resolved conductivity studies of GaAs:As<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>, InGaAs:Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>, InP:O<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> and InP:Fe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup> and relate these results to improved terahertz emitter and detector performance.

articleTitle: Finite element analysis and cryogenic experiment investigation of moving reflector sub-system
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Temperature distribution of moving reflector is obtained by finite element analysis. The cryogenic experimental result has shown that the hypothesis and analysis is reasonable.

articleTitle: Experimental results of high-power, short-pulse, large orbit gyrotron using a pulse power generator "ETIGO-IV"
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: An ultra-high power gyrotron is being developed in millimeter and submillimeter wavelength region. It is a large orbit gyrotron (LOG) with an intense relativistic electron beam (IREB). A pulsed power generator "ETIGO-IV" is used for IREB generation. The prototype LOG with a pulse magnet has been constructed. The first operation test was successfully carried out in millimeter wavelength region. The experimental results are presented.

articleTitle: Antenna Model for Terahertz Cascade Wire Lasers
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Highly divergent radiation is expected from lasers with sub-wavelength apertures due to diffraction. However the short range variations of intensity have been observed in the far field of THz quantum cascade lasers with sub-wavelength apertures. We developed an antenna model for long lasers with subwavelength transverse dimensions (wire lasers). Based on this model we show that the observed far field variations are formed due to the interference of the radiation from the longitudinal mode distribution. We predict that radiation from subwavelength wire laser can be concentrated in a narrow beam with a divergence determined by the ratio of the wavelength to the length of the laser.

articleTitle: THz Surface Plasmon Antennae Experiments
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A diffraction grating engraved in a limited area of a flat aluminum surface serves as coupler to excite surface plasmon that propagates along the flat surface. At the flat surface edge, THz radiation is scattered into free space and impinges the edge of a similar antenna, on which a surface plasmon is excited and diffracted by a grating towards a detector. Using THz time-domain spectroscopy, we study the plasmon-plasmon coupling. We report a strong coupling efficiency over several cm of propagation in air.

articleTitle: Novel Artificial Transmission Line Approach for Synthesis of MMICs for MMW Communications
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A novel error parameter analysis approach for synthesis of an artificial transmission line (ATL) from the ABCD parameters of a uniform transmission line section is presented. An MMIC ATL delay line with 180deg phase shift is synthesized to demonstrate this approach. The MMIC is fabricated using a conventional GaAs process and test results are validated with those of the simulated results.

articleTitle: THz Time-Domain Spectroscopy of Thin-Film DNA Oligomer Having Mismatch
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: THz spectroscopy and imaging is useful for hybridization assessment compared with conventional methods using fluorescence indicators, because THz method can give the hybridization information without any indicators. We have successfully obtained the THz spectrum using 11mers having G-G mismatch and found a very clear peak structure in the spectrum. We also report the THz spectra of 11mers with naphthyridine dimmer binding to G-G mismatch.

articleTitle: Polymerisation-related changes in THz transmission in SU8 and polystyrene
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: THz TDS was used to study the effects of polymerisation on THz transmission in SU8 and polystyrene. SU8 samples, spun onto a THz-transparent polyethelene substrate, were cross-linked to varying degrees using different UV exposure times. Variations in THz absorption and refractive index were observed as a function of the exposure times. Polystyrene samples were prepared as monodispersed powders with varying molecular weights. Variations of the THz refractive index with molecular weight were observed and analysed using the Claussius-Mosotti equation for the dielectric constant.

articleTitle: Electric field tuning of the dielectric response of strontium titanate in the THz range
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We present experimental results evidencing tuning of permittivity by applied electric field in strontium titanate.

articleTitle: A 1-D Multifrequency Non-Linear Model and Simulation for MMW Helix TWTs
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A 1D multifrequency non-linear model of the beam-wave interaction in a millimeter wave helix TWT is described. Taking consideration of the voltage depression, this model has been implemented in a code which contains the functions of scanning beam voltage and input power, convenient for the simulation of the interaction of beam and wave. A MMW TWT interaction is simulated by the code, the results from the code and the comparison with measurements are shown favorably.

articleTitle: THz Spectroscopic Performance Comparison between Micro-Strip-Line Based Sensing Methods and Attenuated Total Reflection
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We have developed compact micro-strip-line-based sensor chips which are appropriate for sensing polar liquids. In order to evaluate the spectroscopic performance of sensor chips, we have compared the absorption coefficients of albumin/water system obtained by the sensor chip with those by the attenuated total reflection method.

articleTitle: Widely Tunable Terahertz-Wave Generation from Collinear Phase-matched GaSe
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Terahertz (THz) wave generation based on the difference-frequency mixing in the GaSe crystal was investigated theoretically and experimentally. An orthogonally polarized dual-wavelength optical parametric oscillator (OPO) with two KTiOPO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> crystals was used as the pump lights. Widely tunable terahertz waves were generated using the collinear phased-matched configuration. The spectral distribution of terahertz-wave intensity revealed the effect of imperfections in the crystal.

articleTitle: Microwave Reflectometry Based On Amplitude Modulation
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Reflectometry is a technique, based on the radar principle, with a response mainly sensitive to the plasma regions where the microwaves are reflected. The reflectometry technique used in plasma devices measures the phase of a wave reflected by a plasma cut-off layer at a given electron density. It has become a promising experimental technique for the measurement of the electron density profile in plasma devices, due to its good spatial and temporal resolution, together with the moderate access requirements and its ability to perform profile inversion along a single line of sight. Since its first implementation on a plasma device for electron density profile measurement, the high cut-off X-mode polarization has convinced many scientists to use this technique on most of the main devices, such as ASDEX, DIII-D, Gamma 10, TJII, TFTR, W7AS etc, and it is planned for edge and scrape of layer profile determination on ITER. HT-7 tokamak is a circular cross-section limiter superconducting tokamak with a 1.22m major radius and 0.27m minor radius. Many experiments such as IBW heating and LHW heating have been conducted in predominantly deuterium target with a toroidal magnetic field BT up to 2.OTesla, plasma current I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sub> up to 200kA and central line averaged electron density n<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sub>(0) = (0.5-6.0)×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">19</sup> m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>. In order to obtain density profiles in these experiments, a microwave reflectometry based on amplitude modulation, is being developed on HT-7 tokamak. The reflectometry was designated according to HT-7 specifications for profile measurements over a rather large range.

articleTitle: Current Collapse Simulation of GaN HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Using a two-dimensional simulator, current collapse effect is simulated in GaN HEMTs. Dynamic picture of trapping of hot electron under gate pulse is discussed. The trapped charge may accumulate under punch-off gate voltage at gate edge drain side due to the large electric Held strain. Self-heating effect is a consequence of the current collapse.

articleTitle: Preliminary Project of the 52 GHz/1 kW/CW Second Harmonic Gyrotron with Permanent Magnet
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The report presents the 52 GHz/1 kW/CW second harmonic gyrotron preliminary design. The gyrotron will be used with appropriate 1 T permanent magnet of FIR Center FU. The possibilities to optimize an electron beam-cavity system are discussed for different gyrotron versions. The influence of cavity mode competition and other effects is investigated also.

articleTitle: III-V Based Semiconductor THz Detectors
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The III-V semiconductor materials have been investigated for use in the terahertz range, and results are reported on heterojunction and homojunction detectors. Broad response out to 1 THz has been observed in both Nitride and Antimonide based detectors. A responsivity R of ~2.5 AAV in 1-5 THz range was observed for a GaN detector. A stronger narrower response was also observed around 6 THz due to impurity ionizations. By changing the Al fraction in the Arsenide based detectors, free-carrier response was adjusted to have a threshold frequency in the range of 2.3-20 THz. Extension of this approach to Antimonide materials could allow free-carrier detectors with thresholds near 1 THz. The mechanisms of operation in these detectors will be discussed, and potential advantages and disadvantages of the materials will be considered. Among these is the increased control in tailoring the workfimction in Antimonides, and increased THz absorption in the Nitrides. The relative advantages of n-vs. p-type structures for the THz region will also be compared. This work was supported in part by the US NSF under grant #ECS-0553051.

articleTitle: Transmission characteristics of 0.3 THz wave using FUCW-I Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The transmission characteristics of 0.3 THz wave through a circular waveguide whose diameter charged from 90 mm to 5 mm by two taper waveguides was investigated. As a power source, FUCW-I gyrotron ( GYCOM, Russia) was used. The gyrotron is operated in CW regime at weak power (20~ 100 W) Gaussian mode with the frequency of 0.3THz. The usual beam current is 130 mA at the accellated voltage 15 KV. The used antenna consists of a Teflon rod dielectric antenna and an insert rod antenna set at 2.4~5.0 mm waveguide. Under the various conditions, the output power from the antenna was measured by water load.

articleTitle: Ternary Amplitude-phase Filter For Hybrid Optronics Scene Matching
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Ternary amplitude-phase filter (TAPF) is proposed here to improve the performance of hybrid optronics scene matching system. We established the system performance evaluation guideline and matching algorithm distortion invariance evaluation guideline by analyzed the influence factors of matching arithmetic. Compared and analyzed several algorithms' performances by Stat, experiment, and the results show that TAPF preserves the information of image's phase and amplitude effectively. TAPF can greatly enhance the anti-noise performance of the system and has good adaptability to bad weathers and improve the probability of scene matching.

articleTitle: Noise Analysis of Brush Scan Long Wave Infra-Red camera
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In this paper we introduce a new noise model based on the 3-D model to analyze the noise character of brush scan LWIR camera with long FPAs.

articleTitle: Design of a Twostage Depressed Collector for Gyrotrons with CHAELOPS
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The paper presents the design of a two-stage depressed collector for 35 GHz gyrotron with a new computer-aided codes - CHAELOPS. The code take into account all three kind of secondary electrons (SE) which is based on Monte-Carlo method. The collector electrode potentials and the magnetic circuit were adjusted to maximize the efficiency of the collector and minimize the effect of SE. The results comparison between EGUN and CHAELOPS has been made and obtained the good agreements. The better collector efficiency was 60% with the total efficiency of gyrotron coming from 20% to 38%.

articleTitle: Propagation of Electromagnetic wave radiated from rotating dipole antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: First, the mathematical theorem about the rotation of polarization vector is presented. From this theorem it is shown that the circular-polarized electromagnetic wave satisfies the Helmholtz equation, but the linear-polarized one doesn't satisfy it. It implies that the latter is not time-harmonic. The observed frequency of the circular-polarized wave radiated from a rotating dipole antenna is also evaluated.

articleTitle: Beam Generation and Transport in THz Tubes
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We present results of 3D simulations of circular and non-circular electron beams for vacuum electronic devices operating at frequencies to 650 GHz. Magnetic and electrostatic lenses and periodic permanent magnet structures will be considered. A typical beam cross section is 150 times 30 microns with 6-8 mA at 10 - 50 keV. Comparison of the calculation with experimental results, as available, will be given.

articleTitle: 0.3 THz Wave Irradiation on Living Bodies through a Catheter Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The development of a 0.3 THz wave catheter for irradiation on living bodies using a gyrotron as the radiation power source is described. Preliminary measurements on the denaturation distribution of irradiated caw livers suggest that they are suitable for common irradiation apparatus for living bodies in similar case as previous report. Transmission tests through catheter waveguides confirm the normal operation of the irradiation apparatus for living bodies.

articleTitle: Upgrade to the ECH System on the DIII-D Tokamak
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A significant upgrade to the 110 GHz DIII-D ECH system was begun in 2005. Two short pulse (< 2 s) GYCOM gyrotrons were replaced by CPI diode gyrotrons having acceptance parameters of 1.0 MW, 5 s and designed pulse length of 10 s. In addition, a CPI gyrotron with depressed collector, which has demonstrated 1.3 MW for short pulses, was installed and is being tested. Two CPI gyrotrons, which have experienced collector failures, are being repaired.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of FSS Structures for Applications in (Sub) millimetre Astronomy Using a PS0 Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a novel procedure for the optimization of band-pass filters consisting of frequency selective surfaces (FSS) embedded in a dielectric. The approach is based on an innovative stochastic algorithm, namely, the particle swarm optimization (PSO), which is integrated into a spectrum domain analysis code.

articleTitle: THz Deformation Modes in Hydrogen-bond Mediated Biomolecular Networks
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The FIR spectra of molecules contain absorption peaks that can serve to identify unknown, illicit or dangerous substances. However, it is still difficult to calculate the absorption spectra of biomolecules in the solid state. We examine the conditions under which a GAUSSIAN modeling becomes realistic by comparing THz TDS and FTIR measurements to DFT results for a set of test molecules.

articleTitle: Terahertz Emission Properties of p-InAs Surface Radiation under Different Excitations
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Terahertz (THz) emission properties of p-InAs surface radiation under the different excitations of femtosecond pulses are studied by means of time-domain spectroscopy. The experimental results show that the spectral waveform and amplitude of terahertz radiation are different for the excitations with different wavelengths. The full-width of half-maximum (FWHM) of THz radiation excited by the short wavelength of pulse is larger than that of the long wavelength. THz emission strength increases with increasing of pump wavelength. The peak amplitude of THz pulse increases linearly with increasing of the excitation power. It provides a useful reference for the application of THz emitter.

articleTitle: Possibility of Injection-Locked Emission of Terahertz Radiation from Grating-Bicoupled Plasmon-Resonant Photomixer
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We experimentally observed terahertz emission of radiation produced by photoinduced plasma instability at room temperature from our original grating-bicoupled plasmon-resonant photomixer. The resonance dominantly excited by dc photocarrier components was enhanced by additionally injected differential-frequency photocarrier components. This indicates a possibility of injection-locked operation for this photomixer.

articleTitle: Characteristic Study of Traveling Wave Tube with Slow Synchronous Wave
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Structure of the traveling wave tube with slow wave system and its dispersion characteristics are analyzed. The influence of slow wave system geometrical sizes on its working capability is discussed.

articleTitle: Analysis of Amphetamine-type Stimulants Tablets by Terahertz Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The components of amphetamine-type stimulant (ATS) tablets were analyzed, and their influence on the terahertz spectra was evaluated. The results suggested the possibility of identifying the components of ATS in tablets by direct terahertz spectroscopy coupled with spectral data processing.

articleTitle: Controlling the cathode current for Performance influence of Oven Magnetrons
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: To reduce spectrum noise of magnetron, the method controlling the cathode current emission is referred by the three dimensional PIC code. Compared three cathode emission model of PIC code in the current control, the beam model is adapts for changing the current. In the appropriate emission current, the spectrum noise can be suppressed.

articleTitle: Influence of slits spacing on the terahertz transmission properties of double sub-wavelength metallic slits
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In this paper, the influence of slits spacing on the terahertz transmission properties of double metallic slits is investigated experimentally. THz TDS is used to measure the transmission properties of two polarized THz radiation (TM polarization and TE polarization). Structures fabricated in the copper film with thickness of 60 mum are examined. For the TE mode, non-resonant transmission features are present. However, the position of the minimal transmissivity can be varied with the slits spacing. In the case of the TM mode, the resonant transmission of the double slits has been demonstrated. Furthermore, it is shown that the position of the resonant peak is related to the slits spacing. This effect may be interpreted as the coupling of THz radiation with waveguide resonances located in the slits.

articleTitle: Research and Design of Terahertz Horn Antenna Based on MEMS Technology
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: This paper studies one kind of new type antenna, which works at about 0.3~1.5THz.The antenna is designed by using FEM (Finite Element Method), and its structure is based on realizable MEMS (Micro-electromechanical Systems) technology. The antenna structure design depends on the physical characteristics of the material Si and the existing technics of MEMS technology. This form of antenna cell is easy to integrate. The simulation result of a 4times4 antenna array is also presented in this paper.

articleTitle: THz sensing method based on thin metallic mesh and an application for bimolecular sensing
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We report on a novel sensing method in the terahertz (THz) range using thin metallic mesh (TMM). Conventionally, the filter property of a TMM can be changed by the geometrical parameters of the TMM. Considering that it is also change when the medium in the vicinity of the mesh openings has a different refractive index, we inspected this principle. For the biomaterial measurements, we deposited the avidin solution uniformly on the TMM. We observed the change of the transmission characteristics.

articleTitle: Spectroscopic s-SNOM powered by infrared frequency-combs
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We report the application of a new type of Fourier-transform spectroscopy called coherent frequency-comb FTIR. This new spectrometer is used to illuminate and read out a scanning mid-infared near-field microscope. The latter is based on an AFM with commercial, cantilevered tips and works on the principle of light scattering; thus it is named scattering or s-SNOM. As a result, we obtain mid-infrared spectra for each pixel of the scanned image. The spatial resolution is typically 30 nm, but 10 nm appears feasible in the near future.

articleTitle: THz pulse propagation in random collections of metal particles
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We report on experimental observations of extraordinary on-axis terahertz transmission through dense collections of metallic particles.

articleTitle: Semiconductor terahertz oscillators and nonlinear dynamics
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We study the negative differential resistance in negative-effective-mass (NEM) semiconductors. The NEM diodes based on the NDR mechanisms have a self-oscillating frequency in the terahertz range. We have investigated the electric domain dynamics in the diodes under dc electric field, and nonlinear dynamics driven by dc+ac voltages.

articleTitle: Rise and Fall Time Behavior of the Gyrotron Backward-Wave Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Axial modes of the gyro-BWO are characterized by a discrete set of optimum transit angles separated by ~2pi. We show in theory that, during the rise and fall portions of the beam pulse, the frequency of a given axial mode varies in such a way that its transit angle remains at the characteristic value of the mode. Furthermore, in this transient period, axial mode competition is governed by the distinctive asymmetry of the mode profiles rather than by levels of the start-oscillation currents. A Ka-band gyro-BWO experiment has been carried out to examine the rise/fall time behavior. Time-frequency analyses of the output pulses show good agreement with theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive Midinfrared Phototransistor
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a highly sensitive phototransistor (14.5 mum). An electrically isolated quantum well (QW) island serves as a photo-sensitive gate (200 times 50 mum) to a nearby two-dimensional conducting channel. Photoelectrons are excited via intersubband transition and escape from the QW, causing the QW to charge up positively. This is, in turn, sensed by the conductance increase in the nearby channel. Reducing the lateral size of the photo-sensitive QW gate (~1 times 1 mum), we achieve photon-counting level sensitivity.

articleTitle: Classification and statistical analysis of skin cancer terahertz spectra
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We are developing computational, statistical pattern recognition tools that allow for the separation of various THz spectral data obtained from normal, pre-cancerous and cancerous tissue.

articleTitle: Scattering of Terahertz Radiation from Random Structures
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A phase distribution function is used to model the optical properties of a randomly structured transmitting layer. The predictions of the model are compared with Mie theory, with previously published experimental data and measurements of the transmission of THz radiation for arrays of cylinders, textiles, powders and glass balls. Overall, satisfactory agreement between the experimental data and theoretical predictions is obtained.

articleTitle: Terahertz generation with two modes working diode laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In this paper, a novel method to generate THz rays by means of duel-mode working laser with external fiber grating cavity is proposed. The new method is based on the second harmonic difference frequency of the two wavelengths.

articleTitle: Effect of the Lossy Layer Thickness of Waveguide Wall on the Small Signal Characteristics of the Gyro-TWT with Distributed-Loss Circuit
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: One of the effective measures for the suppression of spurious oscillations in gyro-TWTs is the use of distributed wall losses generated by coating the waveguide wall with a layer of lossy material with finite conductivity.

articleTitle: Numerical simulation study of two-beam magnetron-injection guns for high powered gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A MIG double-beam gun is presented. The double-beam gun has two annular emitters. When the two beams are injected into the RF system, they can interact with the same mode distribution. The performance of the double-beam Magnetron Injection Gun(MIG) is studied with the particle-in-cell(PIC) code MIGIC for application 35GHz double-beam coaxial gyrotron. In this paper, MIG provide two 70kv, 10Amp beam with the velocity ratio 1.5. Minimum of the transverse velocity spread and the axial velocity spread is about 3%, 5% respectively.

articleTitle: Ka-Band High-Speed Pulsed Modulator
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Using low-barrier Schottky diodes, a Ka-band high-speed pulsed modulator is designed on a finline geometry .The experimental results present that rise time of modulator is less than 450 ps with modulation depth 20 dB or so.

articleTitle: Selective Properties of a Planar Bragg Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We study wave propagation in a open oversized planar waveguide with periodical Bragg structure, translation vector of which is perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation. Such waveguide can be realized either in a medium with periodic modulation of dielectric constant or in planar waveguide with corresponding corrugation. It is shown that step of corrugation phase provides the existence of a mode with exponentially small diffraction losses. This results in high selectivity over transverse indices of considered waveguide.

articleTitle: Laser Difference-Frequency Generation in the Mid-Infrared and Applications to High-Resolution Molecular Spectroscopy and Trace Gas Detection
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We report on the development of a widely tunable continuous-wave (CW) laser spectrometer based on difference-frequency generation (DFG) in a nonlinear optical crystal, which operates in the mid-infrared (MIR) spectral region of 3-20 mum with a Doppler linewidth limited spectral resolution. The state-of-the-art of CW DFG techniques as well as the applications of the DFG-based laser source to high-resolution molecular spectroscopy and trace gas spectroscopy were presented.

articleTitle: Investigation of THz Sommnerfeld Wres for Cavity Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Single wires for surface-wave guiding are currently attracting strong attention as the best performing THz waveguide solution with lowest levels of attenuation and dispersion demonstrated so far. We experimentally investigate the frequency-dependent complex propagation characteristics in the range from 0.02 THz to 0.4 THz. The measured results agree well with our numerical field simulation and confirm the loss mechanisms given by the Sommerfeld theory as valid. We further investigate the application of Sommerfeld wires as guiding element in a compact linear cavity excited by a high-repetition rate femtosecond laser source.

articleTitle: Plasma Wave HEMTs for THz applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: New THz chip solid-state detectors and sources are waited for many applications. The idea of new sources and detectors, based on the oscillations of bidimensional plasma, was theoretically and experimentally demonstrated. We present technological process of nanometric devices dedicated to THz emission. In this structure, a MIM gate-source capacitance is integrated to HEMT to achieve the boundary condition of plasma wave generation and to keep possible the gate biasing, necessary for frequency tuning. High electron mobility material like InAlAs/GalnAs heterostructure is used otherwise the plasma wave is dumped by electron scattering. Electrical and THz measurements are realized.

articleTitle: Fabrications and Characterizations of NbN/AlN/NbN Junctions for THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We present our process for fabricating NbN/AlN/NbN tunnel junctions on MgO substrates. The current-voltage (I-V) characteristics of junctions were measured, and together with the other characteristics in high frequency, especially in the terahertz band.

articleTitle: The Study of Surface Condition of Infrared Thermal Wave Nondestructive technique
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Infrared thermal wave nondestructive detection method is based on the thermal wave theory. Using different heat source to heat the detected material actively, different medium of the material's surface, subsurface physical property and boundary conditions will change the thermal wave's conduction, and then the change will be shown on the surface's temperature field. Through the experimental results and analyse, we can conclude that the infrared thermal wave nondestructive inspection is a feasible method to evaluate the coating and measure the coating thickness.

articleTitle: Plasma Photonics Crystal in Coupled-Cavity Traveling-Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The concept of plasma photonics crystal is presented. The theory of electromagnetic wave propagation in plasma photonics crystal is studied. The plasma density grating is formed by slow wave modulation. From the Maxwell's equations the coupling wave equation can be got and the other electromagnetic field accurate expressions can be got by using the boundary conditions of the coupled-cavity traveling-wave tube(CCTWT).

articleTitle: Modeling a Single Doped Quantum Dot Fiber Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A new kind of dopant-semiconductor nanocrystal (quantum dot) doped into a fiber forming a quantum-dot-doped fiber and thereby configuring a quantum-dot-doped fiber amplifier (QDFA) is presented. The bandwidth, gain and noise of the QDFA is simulated by choosing a kind of PbSe quantum dot with 5.5-nm diameter and solving rate equations in a two-level system. The PbSe-QDFA is obviously advantageous in respects of the bandwidth and noise compared with usual erbium-doped fiber amplifiers available.

articleTitle: Mode Selectivity Enhancement in Cavities of Relativistic Gyrotrons
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In order to guarantee a single-mode regime for high-power relativistic gyrotrons, additional mode selectivity is necessary. It is suggested to substitute the classical cylindrical cavities by conic cavities operating on axis-symmetrical modes. In order to amplify the selectivity, such cavities are supplemented by corrugations, holes, and breaks of diameter.

articleTitle: Latest Tests of a Submillimeter-Wave Backward Wave Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A 600-700 GHz BWO is currently being rebuilt for testing. Previous tests identified problems with the cathode and materials used in the structure. These were addressed and the BWO is now being assembled for testing in July 2006. The modifications to the design are described and test results will be presented.

articleTitle: Study on Effects of Pump Source on Spectra of Optically Pumped Sub-Millimeter Wave Laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In this paper, effects of pump source laser on SMMWL spectra including pump power intensity, pump frequent offset and pump spectral broadening were studied, with TEA CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-9R(16) pumped NH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> 90.4 mum laser used to be an example.

articleTitle: HTS Josephson Junctions for THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Using high temperature superconducting (HTS) Josephson junctions (such as bicrystal Josephson junctions) with a compact dewar, video detections of high frequency signals up to THz range have been demonstrated. Here, the performance as well as the applications in THz wave band for antenna-coupled HTS Josephson junctions are discussed.

articleTitle: THz generation by cascaded optical down-conversion
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We demonstrate THz generation in a cascaded optical down-conversion process, where each optical photon radiates several THz photons. This observation confirms that optical-to-THz conversion efficiency can potentially exceed Manley-Rowe limit imposed by the difference in optical and THz photon energies. The cascade process was observed in quasi-phase matched (QPM) periodic GaAs structures placed in a resonantly pumped optical parametric oscillator. Using a 10W pump laser system, we generated up to 1 mW of THz radiation, tunable in the range 0.5 -3 THz.

articleTitle: Low-Index Discontinuity THz Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A new type of dielectric THz waveguide, which evolved from a recent approach from the held of integrated optics, is presented with theoretical and experimental results. Due to the continuity of electric flux density at a dielectric interface, the THz wave is predominantly confined in the virtually lossless low-index air core of a high-index dielectric waveguide. Attenuation, dispersion, field enhancement and field confinement properties of the waveguide are discussed and compared to those of other THz waveguide approaches.

articleTitle: Sub-Terahertz spectroscopy of superconducting diamond
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In this framework, it has been discovered that boron-doped diamond can also become a superconductor below critical temperatures Tc well above the liquid helium temperature. The strongly covalent bonds, the high concentration of impurities, and the high energy of its optical phonon in comparison with the Fermi energy, make diamond much different from the conventional metals where the BCS theory of superconductivity holds. Here the reflectivity of superconducting diamond is measured down to sub-terahertz frequencies. Our results consistently indicate that diamond, in spite of the above cited peculiarities, behaves as a BCS superconductor in the "dirty" regime.

articleTitle: THz surface polariton plasmons of lef handed materials
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We investigated THz surface polariton plasmon resonance of a left-handed material which has negative dielectric permittivity and negative magnetic permeability. We found that there are two bands of surface plasmon excited by p-polarized wave and, very interestingly, there is one band of surface polariton, magnetic surface polariton, excited by s polarized wave from the simulated reflection spectra. The magnetic surface plasmon resonance is due to the negative permeability. We also discussed that the enhancement of THz transmission through a left-handed material slab by the surface polariton resonance.

articleTitle: Analysis of Surface-Emitted Terahertz-Wave Difference Frequency Generation in Slant-Stripe-Type MgO-Doped Periodically Poled Lithium Niobate
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The theory of THz-wave generation (3.29 THz) via difference frequency generation (DFG) of near infrared radiations (1318.8 nm and 1338.2 nm) by a simultaneous dual-wavelength lasing (SDWL) of an Nd: YAG laser in slant-stripe-type MgO-doped periodically poled lithium niobate (MgO:PPLN) was presented. It is shown that the slant-stripe-type MgO:PPLN is capable of realizing the quasi-phase-matching in two perpendicular direction of optical and THz-wave propagation.

articleTitle: 60GHz Band Planar Dielectric Waveguide Filter with Cross Coupling
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we describe newly developed a vertically stacked and a horizontally arranged dielectric waveguide filter. At the center operation frequency of 59 GHz, the 20 dB bandwidth of the filter is 2.0 GHz, which is almost 4% of the center operation frequency, and the insertion loss is 1.2 dB. The simulation results almost agree with the measured results.

articleTitle: Molecular Coupling of Two Defective Photonic Modes in Two Dimensional Photonic Crystals
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We investigate the coupling property of photonic molecular modes from two defects in two dimensional triangular photonic crystal. We obtain the relationship between the defect modes and its symmetry, and the coupling of the defect modes decreases with the increasing distance between the two defect cylinders. The frequencies of the local defect modes of lowest and highest frequency modes concentrate to the center of the defect modes fully.

articleTitle: Coherent Smith-Purcell Radiation in a Special 3-Mirror Cavity
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Smith-Purcell (SP) effect has been widely used for the generation of the millimeter to infrared wave radiation. The theoretical study and computer simulation on the SP radiation in a special kind of 3-mirror cavity with a grating on the inner surface, a cylindrical mirror, are given in the paper. The results show that it might be a good promising THz radiation source with kW CW power at room temperature.

articleTitle: Monitoring Oxygen Dynamics During Pressure Induced Ischemia on Cancer Xenograft Models
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We recently developed a multi-modal test platform for real time, non-invasive monitoring of tumor tissue structural and oxygen dynamic changes during pressure-induced ischemia. The system integrated a clinical ultrasound, a mechanical load frame, and a near infrared tissue oximeter. The system was tested on an athymic NU/NU mouse model with xenograft pancreatic cancer implanted on the back. The preliminary results demonstrated characteristic differences between the premortem tumor and the postmortem tumor in terms of physical and physiological responses to compression stimuli. These differences suggested that it might be possible to characterize suspicious tumors based on their oxygen dynamic responses to pressure-induced ischemia.

articleTitle: A New Generation of Electron Cyclotron Emission Imaging System for Plasma Diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Electron cyclotron emission imaging (ECEI) is a novel millimeter wave plasma diagnostic technique, which has been extremely successful in the imaging and visualization of electron temperature profiles and fluctuations in magnetic fusion plasma devices. The unique feature of the ECEI diagnostic derives from the use of wideband, low cost planar Schottky diode mixer arrays coupled with innovative, low cost electronics. A new generation of ECE imaging diagnostics is now being developed to extend the current 128-channel system to systems with 256-1054 channels.

articleTitle: Observation of Four-fold Azimuthal Angle Dependence in the Terahertz Radiation Power of (100) p-InAs
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The azimuthal angle dependence of the terahertz (THz) radiation power of (100) p-type In As under 1-T magnetic field is presented. Results exhibited four-fold symmetry for the s-polarized THz radiation power. Moreover, the two-fold symmetry for the p-polarized THz radiation was modified to four-fold symmetry for a 1-T applied magnetic field. A tentative explanation regarding a magnetic field-enhanced L-valley carrier scattering is proposed. The actual physical origin of these results is currently under investigation.

articleTitle: Measurement of Indoor Wideband Millimeter Wave Wireless Channel
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A frequency domain measurement around 60 GHz is described to evaluate the effectiveness of frequency diversity in mitigating the effects of multi-path fading in indoor microcellular channels. The frequency diversity for 150 MHz and other channel bandwidths to accommodate modulated signals with data rates up to 150 Mb/s is presented. Measurements are repeated under identical test conditions. The receive omni-directional antenna replaced by a directional horn to characterize the effect of the receive antenna radiation pattern on the indoor channel.

articleTitle: Drive & Test System for 288 × 4 TDI IRCCD
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The principle and the configuration of a new drive & test system for 288 X 4 TDI IRCCD are presented. It consists of a host-computer-subsystem (HCS) and a slave-computer-subsystem (SCS).
