The SCS is based on the single chip Micyoco and the field programmable gate array. The HCS completes the numerical-parameter input and sends them to the SCS. The SCS implements the parameter adjustment of the derive signal according to the data that are sent from the HCS or stored in the data-store unit. Moreover, the system can implement electronic injection test to the IRCCD. It is validated that some intrinsic defects of the traditional method, such as large size and poor reliability, are eliminated in this method.

articleTitle: A Method to Enhance the Power for CARM Amplifier with Electron Velocity Spread or/and Electron Beam Misalignment
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We present that the power and efficiency for outer-slotted-coaxial waveguide CARM amplifiers can be increased more larger 1 times by the tapering guide magnetic field than those with the uniform guide magnetic field when the electron axial velocity spread or/and electron beam misalignment exist.

articleTitle: Plasma Scattering Measurement using a Submillimeter Wave Gyrotron as a Radiation Source
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Application of an intense, high quality, well-collimated probe beam is effective in improving the performance of the measurement. Such probe beam is produced by stabilization of the high frequency gyrotron output and its conversion into a Gaussian beam.

articleTitle: High-frequency Spin Waves in Aperiodic Multilayer Films
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Summary form only given. We theoretically study the spin waves in an aperioci antiferromagnetic(AF)/ nonmagnetic(NM) multilayer, where the AF layer and the NM layer are arranged in the k-component Fibonacci sequence. The dispersion relation of magnetostatic spin waves and the precession amplitude of the total magnetization are obtained. The multiformity in frequency spectra leads to the tunable spin wave, which may benefit to make tunable devices of spin waves and achieve potential applications on microwave communications.

articleTitle: Sensing Pulsed THz Waves with Ambient Air
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We report the use of air to sense broadband THz waves. Ambient air, with about 79% nitrogen and 21% oxygen, exhibits remarkable performance for the generation and detection of pulsed THz waves with femtosecond laser beams.

articleTitle: Study on photonic crystal reflex klystron for millimeter-wave applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Reflex klystron is employed to demonstrate the possibility of realizing the miniaturized high frequency vacuum devices. To reduce start oscillation current and current density, high order TM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">mno</sub> mode is taken into consideration. Adapting photonic crystal band gap concept, high order mode can be stably supported and coupled to an external system without distortion of the generated mode in the cavity.

articleTitle: Radial line slot array antenna at millimeter wave lengths
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The design and performance of a waveguide-fed linearly polarized radial line slot array antenna is described in this paper. The antenna consists of a rectangular waveguide to radial line coupler and radiating elements. Genetic-algorithm is carried out to optimize the coupler and better performance is obtained. Radiating elements, which are the slots etched on the top plate of the radial line, are designed carefully to radiate linearly polarized wave with low side lobe at millimeter wave lengths.

articleTitle: IR-Spectroscopy in Transient Megagauss Fields
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In IR-magneto optics transient megagauss fields having pulse length in the order of microseconds interact with the sample material not only by the high field value but also by the extremely high dB/dt =10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">8</sup> V/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. These effects are studied in detail in experiment and theory.

articleTitle: Theoretical Study of Dual-wavelength PPKTP-OPO as a Source of DFG THz-wave
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we theoretically investigate the dual-wavelength periodically poled KTP optical parametric oscillator (PPKTP-OPO) operating near degeneracy. According to calculation, the dual-wavelength operation can be achieved by quasi-phase matching with a periodically poled structure. The tunable property of the grating period of the PPKTP crystal with temperature tuning determines that, quasi-CW or continuous tunable THz-wave generation can be achieved by difference frequency generation using a dual-wavelength PPKTP-OPO. Compared with a bulk KTP-OPO operating near degeneracy in theory, the gain property of PPKTP OPO is in better performance, contributing to a higher output power of THz generation.

articleTitle: Portable THz Spectrometers
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We developed a compact and portable THz spectrometer based on millimeter-wave backward wave oscillators combined with frequency multipliers. The instrument operates in frequency range 0.1-1 THz, providing for spectral resolution of 1-10 MHz and dynamic range of at least three orders of magnitude. The system consumes less than 200 W of electrical power and does not require water cooling. Dimensions of the instrument are 70 cm x 40 cm x 35 cm and the weight is less than 40 kg.

articleTitle: Theoretical Investigation of Dual-wavelength Terahertz Wave Generation Based on Slant-Stripe-Type Periodic Poled Lithium Niobate Crystal
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We propose a method for generating dual-wavelength terahertz radiation with a surface emitted configuration based on slant-stripe-type periodic poled lithium niobate (PPLN) Crystal. The crystal is designed to be phase reserved for two difference frequency generation processes so that the predesigned dual-wavelength terahertz radiation at 1.43 THz and 2.07 THz can be achieved simultaneously. The estimated effective nonlinear coefficient as a function of the terahertz radiation frequencies is also included in our discussion. Theoretical analysis shows that the central frequency of the predesigned terahertz radiation will shift inconspicuously due to the permitted fabrication inaccuracy of the crystal period.

articleTitle: Analysis Of a Modified Tunnelandder Slow wave Circuit
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: This article modified the Tunneladder circuit expecting to widen the bandwidth and hope to carry on its merits. In this modified Tunneladder circuit, 'forward-wave' was assumed. Cross-section resembling the idealized unmodified circuit of Tunneladder is analyzed. Through making the longitudinal electronic fields satisfying the boundary condition at one point along the boundary, the dispersing equation and interaction impedance expression of Tunnelplane was derived. Good accordance between theory and HFSS of dispersion characteristics of Tunnelplane is acquired.

articleTitle: Photomixing with LT-GaAsSb Antennas and a Two -Color Nd: LSB Microchiplaser
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We present a new cost-effective two-colour Nd: LaSc<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>(BO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>)<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> microchip laser for photomixing in a low temperature grown (LT) GaAsSb antennas. The generated 700 GHz radiation is detected with a bolometer.

articleTitle: Microwave Radiation from Electric Discharge in Water Medium with Impurities
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Experimental research results of the influence of magnetic field on radiating properties of weak electrolytes in electric discharge. There is a description of experimental model, electrical regimes of the influence on water medium, time realization of discharge processes, the discussion of obtained results.

articleTitle: Applications of Terahertz Techniques to Petroleum Industry
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: With the rapid development of the THz photonic technologies over the past decade, the technologies offer innovative imaging and sensing that can provide information not available through traditional methods. Author expects these technologies to contribute to the petroleum industry:(1) Based on unique absorption fingerprints, THz spectroscopy can be applied in the geophysical and geochemical investigation of well core and related lithologies, organic molecules (such as hydrocarbon), and other chemical substances.(2)Because THz CT is able to reconstruct both the reflective index and density image on both the phase and amplitude of the transmitted THz pulses, the technology can help us to get rich information of oil/gas penetration in the micro-scale core structure.

articleTitle: Two-Color Laser Interferometer using 48- and 57-μm CH3OD Lasers and the Preliminary Experiments
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A two-color interferometer system using 48-and 57-μm CH<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>OD lasers pumped by a continuous-wave (cw) 9R(8) CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> laser have been developed to measure electron density profiles of large plasma devices. To test this system, the Michelson interferometer of one channel has been constructed on a test bench. We have obtained preliminary interference signals from the two-color interferometer system.

articleTitle: The IRMA Water Vapour Radiometer and its Application to Remote Astronomical Site Testing
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: IRMA is a compact, low power, 20um IR water vapour monitor suitable for operation in the astronomical site testing role. IRMA units have been in operation at sites in Chile, Mexico and the USA for the TMT site testing campaign. An additional unit has been modified for operation in the extreme Antarctic environment at Dome C in 2007. We have developed a standalone solar panel/battery power supply and satellite phone based modem control system. This allows an IRMA unit to be powered and operated anywhere on the planet -for example, remote mountain tops in western China that might be suitable sites for telescope construction.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Diagnostics for Vitrification Plants
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Millimeter-wave (MMW) techniques and technologies provide robust new diagnostic tools for glass melt measurements that are addressing needs for vitrification of high level and low activity nuclear wastes in glass media at the Defense Waste Processing Facility (DWPF) in Savannah River and the Waste Treatment Plant (WTP) under construction at Hanford. Over the past seven years, we have demonstrated real-time measurement of several glass melt parameters, e.g., viscosity, cold-cap temperature, foaming, and pouring. An overview of MMW diagnostics for vitrification plants is presented.

articleTitle: Physics basis for the application of electron cyclotron wave system on ITER and its technology
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Electron cyclotron wave system on ITER will be used for plasma start-up heating and current drive. The underlying physics will be outlined. The requirements and the technical aspects of the two launchers will be described.

articleTitle: Optical Properties Of Novel Relaxor-based Single Crystals And Its Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The optical properties of novel electro-optical single crystals (1-x)Pb(Mg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/3</sub>Nb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/3</sub>)O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3-x</sub>PbTiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (PMN-xPT) has been characterized, and their thermal stabilities were investigated.

articleTitle: Nondestructive Testing of Paint Thickness Measurement by Pulsed Infrared Thermography
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In this paper, basic principles of active IR thermography are introduced, paints covered sample is excited by exterior energy with ordinary flashing lamps array, the subsequent change of surface temperature of the sample is monitored by an infrared camera, and sequence of thermal wave signal and data acquisition are processed using the computer, then real-time image signal processing and the analysis were carried on by the special software. Finally using the algorithm, the paint level thickness information can be obtained. The setup of IR NDT system and the new heat excitation-device were presented, especially including creation of key part, i.e. the heat excitation-device which was invented by self in laboratory. Comparing with heating equipment of thermal wave imaging (TWI) imported from US, it has some merits such as lower expense, narrower pulse width, lower power loss and so on.

articleTitle: Development of the Millimeter Wave Diagnostics on HL-2A
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Millimeter-wave technology is widely used in the controlled fusion experiments. In this paper the new diagnostic systems on the HL-2A tokamak, including microwave reflectometry, electron cyclotron emission, was presented. The new methods for plasma particle transport and the experiments on HL-2 A tokamak was shown. The plans of the diagnostic development in next step are also presented.

articleTitle: Compact X-Band High Gradient Photoinjector and Accelerator for Compton Scattering
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The advent of X-band vacuum technologies has allowed for the construction of compact electron beam sources able to deliver 60 MeV ultra-short bunches previously only realizable in large scale national laboratories. Using a novel frequency selection scheme a titantium: sapphire laser oscillator serves as both optical source for the photoinjector and master clock for the microwave components. Additionally the table-top laser amplifiers, also seeded by the oscillator, are inherently synchronized to the RF sources. This allows for a simplified collinear Compton scattering X-ray source tunable from 10 to 80 keV. Successful operation of the system has demonstrated initial signs of Compton X-rays.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Characteristics of Gyro-TWT with Helical Corrugation
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The rule of mode coupling and mode competition in helical wave-guide are analyzed according to the coupling wave equations of it. The selection of operating point is discussed. These provide basis for the calculation of beam-wave interaction.

articleTitle: Room Temperature, Low Threshold Distributed Feedback Quantum Cascade Lasers at 7.7 μm
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we present low threshold DFB QCLs (λ ≡ 7.7 μm) with top grating by innovating the waveguide structure and the method of grating fabrication. Highly doped InP cladding layer was taken as the host layer for the grating, and was anisotropically etched along [O<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-</sup><sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub>] direction with the lateral etching being negligible. This method releases the limitation on the grating depth. By careful design and control a deep first-order grating, with a thin highly doped InP layer beneath it, was formed in the plasmon enhanced cladding layers. The deep grating ensures strong feedback effect and the thin highly doped InP layer separates the high loss metals in the groove of the grating from the active region, suppressing the increase of the waveguide loss. It allows the fabrication of DFB QCLs with low threshold current density.

articleTitle: Efficiency Enhancement of Optically Pumped FIR Laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In the present paper, role of FIR cavity and output coupler in degrading the efficiency of OPML is discussed. To enhance the efficiency, a novel structure for FIR cavity with output coupling slots is simulated using HFSS. Simulated result shows significant improvement in efficiency.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wavelength Nonlinear Excitation for Vanishing Anisotropy of Planar Hexaferrite
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In the past decades, nonlinear excitations of magnetic systems under microwave fields were widely studied by experimental and theoretical investigations of high power microwave parallel pumping. Hexaferrite may be the only choice for THz applications of magnetic materials in modern technology. However, its applications are limited because of high power requirements and bulkiness. In order to solve these issues, we present a model for the controllable basal plane anisotropy field of planar hexaferrite, which is able to create an environment for nonlinear excitations in ordinary power applications of microwaves. We also present the micron size ferrite resonator's geometrical effect on the excitations.

articleTitle: Characterization of InAs/GaAs quantum dots utilizing THz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We have investigated the carrier capture behavior of n-type modulation-doped InAs/GaAs QDs using THz time-domain spectroscopy (THz TDS) in order to estimate the total number of electrons captured by the QDs. The THz transmission of the sample with QDs (#1) is larger than that of the sample without QDs (#2). From the THz waveforms and subsequent analysis, the #1 sample shows lower conductivity which is resulted from the smaller number of free carriers due to the capture by the QDs.

articleTitle: Analysis and Synthesis of Mirrors for High Divergence Microwave Beams
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The Katzenelenbaum-Semenov-Algorithm for the analysis and synthesis of microwave beams is commonly used e.g. in transmission lines and gyrotrons for plasma heating. However, this algorithm is limited to flat mirrors (corresponding to thin lenses) and paraxial beams. The paper describes a method for the analysis and synthesis of deep mirrors (corresponding to thick lenses) as used e.g. for quasi-optical mode converters in gyrotrons. The opportunity to also sythesize deep mirrors gives an additional degree of freedom. It can improve the beam quality and/or reduces the required number of mirrors for a given beam transformation when non-paraxial beams are involved.

articleTitle: Nano-scale Metamaterials: Fabrication and Optical Measurements from THz towards visible
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We have designed, fabricated, and optically measured several different nano-scale metamaterials. We employ e-beam nano-lithography technology at LBNL's CXRO for fabricating these structures on extremely thin SiN substrates so that they are close to free-standing. Optical properties were measured as a function of incidence angle and polarization using the ALS synchrotron IR beamlines. We directly observe strong magnetic resonances consistent with negative magnetic permeability in our samples at THz through near-IR optical frequencies. We will compare the results to detailed simulations. Finally, we will report on our progress towards constructing a negative index of refraction nano-scale metamaterial.

articleTitle: Study of Tunable Terahertz-Wave Generation in Isotropic Semiconductor Crystals Based on Dual-Wavelength KTP-OPO Operating near Degenerate Point
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Continuously tunable coherent terahertz-wave generation from 0.1 to 2.7 THz can be achieved in isotropic semiconductor nonlinear crystals by difference frequency mixing. We experimentally demonstrated a high-power, narrow-linewidth, angle-tuned pulsed dual-wavelength KTP-OPO operating near the degenerate point, which was used as the pump source for terahertz-wave generation. We theoretically studied the feasibility of the cross-Reststrahlen band dispersion compensation phase matching in the collinear optical mixing technique in this process. A theoretical analysis of perfect phase-matching conditions and coherence length for the ZnTe crystal was presented, according to its optical dispersion property.

articleTitle: The Effect of the Signal Correlation on the Array of Synthetic Aperture Microwave Radiometer
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The signal correlation, the key problem in the technology of Synthetic Aperture Microwave Radiometer (SAMR), is analyzed in detail. Firstly, the expression of the microwave signal passing through the front of radiometer is deduced. Secondly, the signal correlation of SAMR is analyzed, with the conclusion that the signal correlation has a strong effect on the array.

articleTitle: The Study of the Terahertz Spectral of LiNbO3 Crystal
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The absorption coefficient and refractive index of the LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (LN) crystal have been obtained in the range of 0.4-1.6 terahertz (THz) by terahertz time domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS).

articleTitle: Theoretical Analysis of Broadband Source by Using Retracing Behavior of Collinear Quasi-Phase-Matching Optical Parametric Generator
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: According to the concept of phase matching bandwidth the band width of broadband source by using retracing behavior of collinear quasi-phase-matching (CQPM) optical parametric generator (OPG) in periodically poled lithium niobate (PPLN) is presented firstly. Comparing the various pump wavelengths we obtain the pumping condition and parameters of PPLN to realize the broadband source near 1550 nm in the CQPM-OPG. In theory we present the optimum pump wavelength and the maximum ideal bandwidth range to be 940.75 nm and 14751681 nm respectively.

articleTitle: A novel two-channel correlation radiometer
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A novel Ka-band two-channel correlation radiometer with independent local oscillator is constructed. To remain coherence in phase between two channels, the frequency of local oscillator must be very stable. The difference of phase between two channels, which is approximately invariable in a period of time, can be compensated by digital signal algorithm, so complexity of hardware can be reduced obviously.

articleTitle: Study of Laser-induced Damage in the Material of THz Wave Generator
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Pulse laser of 1064 nm damage studies are performed in two kinds of material. One is the MgO:LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> for using in THz parameter generator system, and another is the Si-GaAs material for using in THz photoconductive antenna. All the experiments were performed in the bulk of material, which irradiated by Nd:YAG Q-switch laser beam with nanosecond pulse. In the case of the LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, the damage is associated with both the self-focusing inside the material, and the thermal damage on the face. As for the GaAs, the material damage can be divided into two types of the un-reparable and reparable.

articleTitle: Preparation of CdSe Quantum Dots and Characterization of Single CdSe Quantum Dots
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Tne photoluminescence of CdSe quantum dots with different diameter were studied in toluene and on silicon substrate. Single CdSe quantum dot was prepared through a simple method, which was conformed by AFM images.

articleTitle: Terahertz Polarization Imaging using <110> ZnTe Crystal
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We present a method to measure the polarization state of pulsed terahertz wave by using a typical electro-optic sampling setup with <110> ZnTe crystal as sensor. To illustrate that the knowledge of the polarization of the terahertz pulse is essential for interpreting the results, we did terahertz imaging of a plastic plate. We find the terahertz electric field vector is revolved by the scattering at the edge of the sample. Terahertz polarization imaging is sensitive to the edge of the object and therefore can be used to raise the spatial resolution and improve the quality of terahertz images.

articleTitle: The Optical Properties of scintillation PbWO4 crystal doped with BaF2
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The transmittance spectrum along c axis of the BaF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>:PbWO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> crystal expressed the higher transmittance than that of pure PbWO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> crystal. The luminescence intensity of the peak at 400~450 nm in X-ray excited luminescence spectrum of the BaF<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>:PbWO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> crystal was increased significantly, about 2 times higher than that of pure PbWO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub>.

articleTitle: Measurement of Minority Carrier Lifetime in Hg1-xCdxTe Photodetector
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The transient photo-generated excess minority carrier lifetime in Hg1-xCdxTe n+p junction photodetector are measured using improved photo-induced open-circuit voltage decay (OCVD) technique. The lifetimes we extracte from the decay curve of the photovoltage are from tens to hundreds ns. A comparison of the relationship between composition of Cd and minority carrier lifetime show the lifetimes become longer with the increasing of Cd composition.

articleTitle: Experimental and Theoretical Study of the Terahertz Absorption Spectra of Crystalline Saccharides
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy has been used to measure the full dielectric function of polycrystaltine D-glucose and D-mannose. A number of well-resolved absorption peaks were observed in the frequency range 0.2-3.0 THz, which are interpreted as originating from inter-and intra-molecular vibrational modes. In parallel with the experimental study, density functional theory was applied to obtain structure and vibrational frequencies of the saccharides. The calculated results are in reasonable agreement with the experimental data. The comparison between experimental and theoretical study shows that far-infrared absorption features are highly sensitive to the structure and spatial arrangement of molecules.

articleTitle: Computer Optimized Gun Design
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Computer optimization can explore a wider parameter space than practical with manual design, particularly for 3D geometries. This allows rapid, economical development of higher performance devices. The proliferation of parametric solid modeling programs allows optimization of both geometry and operating parameters. This presentation described computer optimization in the 3D trajectory code beam optics analysis (BOA). This is possible because meshing in BOA is completely automatic, allowing the program to be controlled by the optimization routines.

articleTitle: Simulation and optimization of the package joints in the Quantum well infrared photodetectors Focal Plane Array
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In hybrid IR FPAs, infrared photodetectors and Si read out integrated circuits (ROICs) are bonded together with indium bumps by flip-chip bonding. The heat-force coupling field of the package joints between infrared photodetectors and ROICs is simulated based on finite-element analysis (FEA) software for finding strain position of the bump and optimizing, and reducing fatigue.

articleTitle: Investigation of Pico-Second Triggered Jitter-Time Ultra-Fast Electrical Pulses with GaAs Potoconductive Switches
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The generation of triggered jitter-free ultra-fast electrical pulses is important in precise and ultra-fast bing bang control. Experiments of a lateral semi-insulating GaAs photoconductive semiconductor switch triggered by nanosecond laser pulse were reported. The switches were insulated by solid multi-layer transparent dielectrics. Jitter-free electrical pulse from the 1 mm-gap GaAs switches was observed when biased with the low voltage and triggered by the serial laser pulses. Its triggered jitter-time was less than 10 ps, and pulse width was up to sub-nanosecond.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of an Injection-Locking Gyrotron Backward-Wave Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Controlling the phase and frequency of a gyrotron backward-wave oscillator (gyro-BWO) by means of injection-locking techniques is of practical importance. Using a nonlinear self-consistent time-independent code, this study analyzes the stability of a gyro-BWO with an external injection signal. To examine the stability of steady-state solutions, the perturbation of the phase difference between the oscillator and injected signal must decay in time.

articleTitle: Analysis of RF Field in Open Cavity by Mode-Matching Technique
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Open cavity with abrupt changes is generally used in the gyro-oscillators and amplifiers. On the basis of mode-matching technique we present the high frequencies structure analyses code for gyrotron. The code provides a method for computing the resonant frequency and Q value in an open cavity. We present the theory and an example which demonstrates the operation and the possible usage of the code.

articleTitle: Electronic charge pumping in superlattice nanowire under pulsed signals
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: By applying pulsed signals on two point of a superlattice nanowire with phase difference phi, the induced current is calculated theoretically. The method is based on defining all the operators in the Hilbert space of side band states defined in terms of Floquet theorem. Using this method, we have calculated the electronic transport as a function of phase difference of applied signals. It is shown that for special phase difference the polarity of induced current is changed.

articleTitle: Enhanced Terahertz Emission from InAs Quantum Dots on GaAs
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Optically pumped THz emission has been observed in a wide range of semiconductors, and this process is an important practical source of pulsed THz radiation for time-domain THz spectroscopy and THz imaging. We show that InAs quantum dots on GaAs can be used to significantly enhance THz emission compared with a bare GaAs surface.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Delay-time for Wideband SI-GaAs Photoconductive Antenna Triggered by Laser Pulse
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In this paper, we reported the delay-time measurement experiments for a biased semi-insulating gallium arsenide photoconductive antenna, triggered by laser pulse, and performed at the nonlinear model. The electromagnetic wave output character dependence of the delay-time is analyzed by using the Fourier transforms spectrum. The delay-time at the excited laser pulse of 532 nm and 1064 nm were measured. We observed a huge delay-time of hundreds microsecond when triggered by 1064 nm laser at the specific biased-voltage conditions. The analysis indicated the huge delay-time relate to the photogenerated carriers translation between the different energy states of EL2 deep energy level.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave propagation and heat radiative effect in metal particle cloud
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Metal particle cloud is a mixture of micrometer-size metal spheres and air. We investigate the electromagnetic wave propagation and the heat emission of metal cloud. Because of large scattering and low emission in infrared region, it can be applied in airspace technology.

articleTitle: A Modified Millimeter-Wave Frequency Multiplier
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A novel millimeter FET frequency multiplier is presented. It works in a way similar with the resistive mixer to generate multiple harmonics and adopts proper reflector networks in the input/output networks to improve the performance. The configuration has the great stability characteristic in addition to zero DC power dissipation, and it is not sensitive to the input signal power. The analysis and the preliminary measurement show that the conversion efficiency of -5 dB is obtained, with the output frequency being 35 GHz.

articleTitle: Selective growth of II-VI materials on Si(211): First-principle calculations
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Using the First-principle calculation software, the adsorptions of CdTe layers and ZnTe layers on the clean and As-passivated Si(211) substrates are simulated respectively. Based on the computational results, we theoretically interpret the important effects of the As<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> passivation during the epitaxial growth: arsenic can saturate part of the dangling bonds and weaken the surface states to make the discrepancy of the substrate surface, which induce the B-face polarity selection automatically. This conclusion can provide further explanations for the successful growth of large area high quality CdTe(211)B layers on the Si(211) surfaces.

articleTitle: Vavilov-Cherenkov radiation in a Photonic Crystal
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Theoretical study and computer simulation on the Vavilov-Cherenkov radiation (VCR) in one dimensional (1D) and two dimensional (2D) photonic crystals are given in the paper. A variety of interesting and important behaviors for the VCR in a 2D photonic crystal have been revealed previously, such as the backward VCR may occur when the electron energy is lower than the threshold, etc.(Chiyan Luo, 2003). Some new important features of the VCR in photonic crystals have been observed and the physical mechanism is studied as well. The possible applications of the VCR in crystal are discussed.

articleTitle: FITD Simulation of Terahertz Near-Field Microscopes
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The spatial resolutions of conventional THz TDS systems are limited by diffraction. In this work, we present a numerical analysis of apertureless THz pulse near-field microscopy (NFM), and successfully demonstrate that the THz NFM can have nanometer-scale resolution. For the numerical analysis we used CST MWS, a commercial software based on finite integral time domain (FITD) method. It is found that the THz near field is strongly localized around the probe tip as expected, which is of importance for nanometer resolution.

articleTitle: Design of Multiple Beams Forming Network for Switched Beam Antenna System with E - Shaped Microstrip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: This paper presents the design of multiple beams generation by switched beam antenna systems employing an E-shaped microstrip antenna. The designed antennas have bandwidth of 20%, 32% and 45% and gain of 8 dB, 10 dB and 12 dB respectively with single, 2 and 4 element antennas.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Mechanism of Terahertz Radiation from InAs under Magnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The magnetic field dependence of terahertz radiation from InAs excited by femtosecond laser pulses has been measured with the time-domain spectroscopy up to 10 T. The magnetic field dependence of n-InAs shows a radiation power minimum around 5 T whereas p-InAs does not show such a minimum. Additionally, it is found that the polarity of the amplitude of terahertz radiation is reversed at 5 T for n-InAs. This polarity reversal is attributed to a crossover of the radiation mechanism from the photo-Dember effect to magnetoplasma oscillations with increasing magnetic field.

articleTitle: Millimeter wave irradiation and invasion into living bodies using AR waveguide vent antennas
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The microwave invasion into living bodies at a millimeter wave catheter irradiation is described. The power sources of millimeter wave are an Impatt oscillator (94 GHz, 0.3 W) for the irradiation tests, a Gunn oscillator (90 GHz, 13 mW) for the reflection study, and a gyrotron for high power irradiation. Irradiated samples are cow livers and living rats. In the newly designed irradiation antennas, a part of the copper waveguide is replaced with the flexible Teflon rod.

articleTitle: An Investigation on Spectral-Characteristic of HgCdTe two-color Detector
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Some recent results of spectral-characteristic investigation on integrated HgCdTe infrared two-color detector are presented. Many discussions were focused on SWIR response of the preliminary two-color detector which exhibited a sharply peaked spectrum. The reason of SWIR abnormal spectrum was rooted out, and the way to solve the problem was obtained theoretically. Finally, the proper spectral responses of two-color detector with an improved structure were accomplished as expected.

articleTitle: Application of a Membrane Device for Biosensing with Terahertz Time Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We propose a novel device relying on a membrane used in life sciences for analyzing the terahertz (THz)-wave transmission characteristics of biomolecular samples. This device allows small amounts of sample to be prepared easier than current methods. We prepared several sugar samples adsorbed on the membrane, and measured them using THz time domain spectroscopy. The THz absorption data were found to be different depending on the concentration of samples, which demonstrates the potential of the membrane device in THz-wave biosensing applications.

articleTitle: Two-Beam Instability for THz Radiation Source
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Theoretical study and digital calculations on the two beams instability in a cylindrical waveguide by a finite axial magnetic field for THz radiation source have been given in the paper. In our approach the electron beams are considered the moving non-neutralized plasma and the surface current due to the ripple of electron beams are taken into consideration in the analysis of beam-wave interactions. With the boundary conditions, the dispersion equation was obtained and solved numerically. The results show that under certain conditions, THz radiation may be achieved.

articleTitle: Coherent Transmission of THz Wave through Randomly Packed Subwavelength-sized Aluminium Particles
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In the experiments of THz wave transmission through an ensemble of randomly packed aluminium particles with subwavelength sizes, we observed a strong dependence of the transmission on the lateral boundary conditions. Our results clearly showed that the processes of THz wave re-emitting from the disk-shaped samples were pure surface modes, and it is critically affected by properties of the side interface and the diameter of samples.

articleTitle: The Primary Design of ECU for EAST
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: EAST, a non-circular superconducting tokamak device, is to realize stable operation and carry out advanced operational mode. ECH system is one of the most important plasma heating and current driving methods for EAST. After referring to ECH systems operating on the other devices all over the world, a primary design of ECH for EAST will be provided according to the main parameters and physical experiment plan on EAST. This ECH system mainly consists of gyrotron, cooling water system, transmission line (MOU, waveguide, miter bends, switchers, polarizer, vacuum valve and ion pump, DC breaker, power measurement, power monitor), dummy load, launcher, high voltage power supply (HVPS) and control system.

articleTitle: The Cylindrical Taylor-Interpolation FFT Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The cylindrical Taylor-Interpolation FFT (TI-FFT) algorithm for the computation of the near-field and far-field in the "quasicylindrical" geometry has been developed. The cylindrical modal expansion of the vector potential is shown to be in the form that can make use of the cylindrical TI-FFT. The near-field on an arbitrary cylindrical surface is obtained from the vector potential and through the Inverse FFT (IFFT). The far-field is obtained through the Near-Field Far-Field (NF-FF) transform. The cylindrical TI-FFT is valuable for back-scattering problems and "quasi-cylindrical" geometry. Like the planar TI-FFT algorithm, the cylindrical TI-FFT algorithm also has advantages of a N2 log2 N2 computational complexity, a low sampling rate, no basis functions and free of singularity problems.

articleTitle: Physical Optics Modeling for the Optimization of Millimetre-Wave Personnel Scanners
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Recent advances in mm-wave imaging show promise for the enhanced detection of threats hidden under clothes. This is particularly important for airport security. This paper focuses on a methodology, based on a comprehensive simulation of the physics of an imaging system, that aims to assess the potential of various modifications to the current systems. This offers low-cost and rapid exploration of the effects of various system parameters, such as imager polarization manipulation, frequency, coherence parameters etc. We report here on the effect of frequency on scene contrast.

articleTitle: Using Photonic Technique for Emitting Millimeter Wave Signals
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A photonic transmitter using millimeter wave (MMW) photonic techniques is proposed. As for the MMW generation, a 75 GHz generator is developed to get both pulse trains and sinusoidal signals. Electronic MMW amplifier in high power photonic MMW emitter is replaced by using a unitraveling carrier (UTC) photodiode. The UTC photodiode output power generated by a narrow pulse train is higher than that generated by sinusoidal signals under the same average optical power condition, which contributes to reducing the photocurrent of the photonic emitter. The proposed photonic transmitter can be applied to the optical gigabit Ethernet signals in the wireless link system.

articleTitle: Development of a Compact Instrument using Fiber Laser based Difference-Frequency Generation Source for Chemical Gas Detection
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We describe the development of a compact instrument for trace gas detection of chemical species. The instrument, operating in the mid-infrared (3.16 -3.41 mum), is based on continuous-wave fiber laser pumped difference-frequency generation in a PPLN crystal. Development and application of this novel laser instrument to spectroscopic sensing of chemical trace gas will be presented.

articleTitle: THz superconducting hot electron bolometer heterodyne receivers
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We will highlight recent progress in superconducting NbN hot electron bolometer (HEB) mixers achieved through close collaboration between SRON and TU Delft.

articleTitle: Terahertz Generation and Domain Mapping in Periodically Poled Crystal
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We measured multi-cycles of ps electric pulses (THz waves) generated by optical rectification in a periodically poled LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (PPLN) crystal using an electro-optic ZnTe detector of 1.55 mm-length. The input energy of fs pulse is about 160 uJ and its pulse duration is about 150 fs. The 2 mm-long PPLN crystal has the domain period of 30.8 mum. We found that the THz waves generated in the PPLN crystal always contained those generated in the bulk LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> crystal. Multi-cycles of sub-ps electric pulses generated in the periodic domains allow us to map the distribution of the domain length directly. From the successful domain mapping, we confirmed that the sub-ps electric pulses were due to THz waves propagating reversely to the fs pump pulse, backward waves. No observation of the THz waves propagating parallel with the pump pulse, forward waves, was caused by the detection limit of our thick ZnTe crystal in high THz frequency range.

articleTitle: Electrics Characteristic of Terahertz Generation with GaAs Photoconductive Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Experiment of terahertz generation with photoconductive dipole antenna based on semi-insulating GaAs is researched. Terahertz waveform with about 1 ps width is observed. The frequency spectrums of the terahertz radiation range over 1 THz, and their peaks are at roughly 0.3 THz. The electrics characteristic of GaAs simulated using the finite difference time domain method is presented.

articleTitle: Alternative Free Energy Model of Millimeter Wave Hexaferrite
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We have developed a new free energy model of hexaferrite for the theory of ferromagnetic resonance by Kittel. This study showed that by using this free energy model we were able to derive resonance conditions for M and Y-types. In addition to that we were able to present the angle dependence of the basal plane anisotropy field of Y-type. In order to show that our theory is applicable to other hexaferrites, we also present our results for W and Z-type. Throughout this paper millimeter wave susceptibilities are discussed in terms of Polder manner. This is a unique model for MMW hexaferrite.

articleTitle: Studies of BaO-Nd2O3-TiO3 thin films by RF Sputter and its TMLs
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: As a high permittivity and low loss ceramic, BaO-Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>-TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> (BNT) is widely used in millimeter wave dielectric resonator. Perfect BNT thin films are obtained by through high density plasma RF sputter, and compared dielectric properties with bulk. The results show that underlay temperature has mainly effect on thin films. The optimize technology is gotten. Through simulation, thin film microstrip line based on BNT has more high integration and more excellent microwave dielectric loss properties than standard microstrip Line.

articleTitle: Experimental and Theoretical Study of THz Radiation in Far Field Generating from GaAs Large Aperture Photoconductive Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: THz radiation intensity of GaAs large aperture photoconductive antenna dealt with insulation technique is increased by one order. The time domain waveform of far field generated from the antenna is made out by simulation, based on the current surge model. The influences of current carrier's mobility and lifetime to THz radiation power are discussed.

articleTitle: Development of X-band Magnetic Resonance Force Microscopy
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We report the modification of a X-band magnetic resonance force microscopy probe at our research center. We have newly developed a 3D(xyz)-piezo stage, which is made of titan, graphite, and commercial multilayer piezoelectric actuators. This piezo stage enables nanopositioning of a optical fiber and a sample at very low temperatures, and 3D scanning measurements. To achieve the higher spatial resolution, we have added the frequency stabilization system, which controls the microwave frequency within Deltaf ~100 kHz.

articleTitle: Terahertz Photoconductive Folded Dipole Antennas
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Photoconductive three-wire folded dipole antennas for terahertz photomixers have been developed. The folded dipole antennas have much higher antenna resistance than other resonant dipole antennas, implying that they can be used for higher output power of THz photomixers.

articleTitle: THz near-field microscopy - A review
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: One of the major limitations of THz imaging is low spatial resolution. Consequently, various techniques have been proposed in the literature to break the diffraction limit. Many of the existing techniques draw inspiration from near-field scanning optical microscopy, while other techniques tightly focus optical beams to reduce the size of the generated THz beams. This paper reviews briefly the existing THz near-field methods and recent developments for identifying possible areas of research potential.

articleTitle: Terahertz Time-Domain and Raman Studies of Sulfur-Containing Polypeptides
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We present the THz and Raman spectra of sulfur-containing di-and tetrapeptides in the form of molecular polycrystalline powder and in solution. The spectra measured in far-infrared region with the use of terahertz (THz) time-domain spectroscopic technique. The spectral features in THz and Raman spectra are different among sulfur-containing di-and tetrapeptides. We are discussing the possibility to observe and to assign the low-frequency THz and Raman lines to the disulfide bridges. The experimental results are compared with ab initio calculations to discuss assignment of the vibrational modes. In addition the possibility to observe the low frequency the molecular motions in native liquids and the mixtures is discussed.

articleTitle: Far Infrared Characterization of Semimagnetic Semiconductor CdTe-Cd1xMnxTe Multi Quantum Wells
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: By using a macroscopic model based on effective medium theory, we have analyzed the s-and p-polarized far infrared magnetoplasmon spectra of doped CdTe-Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Mn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Te multi quantum wells in the presence of a static magnetic field parallel to surface of layer. The results show the transverse optical modes (for whole composition range, x= 0 to 1) are sensitive and change linearly with respect to composition parameter. Also, the analysis of tensor of dielectric function and Voigt dielectric function are used to determine carrier's effective masses (hole and electron) as a function of composition. The results are compared with data from Raman and far infrared measurements.

articleTitle: Time-domain THz spectroscopy (TDS-THz) of bovine rhodopsin in solution
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We have recorded THz spectra for prepared samples of bovine rhodopsin. These spectra have been used to generate difference spectra in order to look for evidence of the structural transformation which occurs in this molecule after illumination with light in the wavelength range 500 nm-800 nm.

articleTitle: Time-domain spectroscopy of THz quantum cascade lasers: Theoretical and experimental aspects
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We present fully developed model of the time-domain spectroscopy of the terahertz gain medium. Based on this model we simulated pulse amplification and the coherent response of the gain medium. We show that except of generally expected amplification of the pulse after interaction with the gain medium, other effects like the spectral shaping, spectral 'hole burning', and the phase coherence revival typical for the pump/probe technique are directly observable in the time domain signal. This unique measurement technique is further discussed with respect to the probing terahertz quantum cascade structures and we draw the theoretical limits of them to amplify the broadband (ps long) pulses.

articleTitle: Electrode's Match Design of High Power Ultra-wideband Photo-conductive Switch for Particular Trigger Conditions
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Non-uniform illumination near the anode of photoconductive switch can produces ultra-fast electric pulse. As the rise of laser pulse power for more powerful electric pulse, the transient absorbability of anode descends along with process of electric absorbing. Indeed, a rejected electric field forms near the anode. To reduce this phenomenon and obtain more powerful ultra-fast electric pulse, electrode's match design method for particular trigger conditions based space-charge effect is mentioned in this paper.

articleTitle: Accuracy Analysis of Full Digital Compensatory Millimeter Wave Radiometer
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: MMW radiometer is the core equipment of passive MMW remote sensing. As a new type of radiometer, full digital compensatory MMW radiometer can compensate system gain and receiver noise fluctuation by using digital compensatory algorithm. According to the designed full digital compensatory 8mm radiometer, the accuracy analytical method of the designed MMW radiometer system is put forward in this paper.

articleTitle: A new low-emissivity films Prepared by Magnetron Sputtering
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Low-emissivity (Low-E) films, which have low transparence in near infrared region, are prepared by RF magnetron reactive sputtering and DC sputtering in turn as the structure of air/TiO2/Ti/Ag/TiO2/ on the glass. Titanium layer protection Ag layer from being oxidized is observed. The transmittance of low-E films was measured by spectrophotometer. The Low-E films can get a best transmittance, while the thickness of titanium layer is about 1 nanometer. In the visible region (380 nm - 780 nm), the highest transmittance is up to 82.4%, and the average transmittance is 75%. In the near infrared region (780 nm - 2500 nm), the average transmittance is 16.2%.

articleTitle: Moderate-Power W-Band Cerenkov Traveling-Wave Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A compact W-band (95 GHz) traveling-wave amplifier design is discussed, in which the slow wave circuit consists of a smooth rectangular waveguide with ceramic dielectric lined side walls. Small-signal performance for the 15-kV, 0.33-A device is predicted to include 30-dB gain for a 7.4-cm long circuit, ~500 W output, 2 GHz instantaneous bandwidth, and 13 GHz voltage-tunable bandwidth. A 2-3 kG solenoidal magnetic field is required for beam focusing. Rectangular geometry for the slow wave circuit allows for longitudinal splitting of the circuit, thus permitting precision fabrication and suppression of non-symmetric competing modes.

articleTitle: Investigation of Diffusion Processes by THz Time-Domain Reflection Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Liquid diffusion in polymers has been studied for the first time using terahertz (THz) time-domain reflectance spectroscopy. We show that both the position and movement of the liquid diffusion front through the polymer as a function of time can be quantified. These data are validated by comparison with the same quantities measured using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).

articleTitle: THz Fingerprinting of Biomolecules Supported by Ab Initio Molecular Modelling
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In this paper we explore various ab initio molecular approaches and their usefulness for the prediction of vibrational spectra of biomolecules.

articleTitle: Real-Time THz Imaging of Large Objects based on the Triangulation Method
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We have built a THz Imaging setup for large objects where "large" is defined as "too big to fit on an optical table". THz radiation is focused on the object, and the radiation reflected or scattered under a finite angle is recorded with a CCD camera via EO sampling in real time. If an object has multiple reflecting or scattering surfaces, all of them cause different THz spots on the EO crystal, and the position of such a spot immediately reveals the 3D position of the illuminated area on the respective surface.

articleTitle: THz Coherent Vavilov-Cherenkov Radiation in a Special 3-Mirror Cavity
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The study of THz radiation sources is one of the most attractive and important topics in modern science and technology. Theoretical study and computer simulation of the THz Vavilov-Cherenkov radiation (VCR) in a 3-mirror cavity are presented in the paper. The 3-mirror cavity was specifically developed based on the Fabry-Perot cavity, it may greatly increase the output power and improve the coherence of the radiation through collecting the emission of the radiation in the entire solid angle of the radiation direction at a resonant mode of the cavity. Under coherent conditions the VCR of electron bunches excites one of the resonant modes in the cavity. For 4.41 dielectric permittivity and 180 keV electron beam, the VCR at 0.8 THz was obtained.

articleTitle: THz Radiation from Alternating Current Josephson Effect
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: An assumption and fundamental theory of radiating terahertz (THz) electromagnetic wave with a superconductor-insulator-superconductor (SIS) junction have been discussed using alternating current Josephson effect. According to the experiment in BSCCO, it is possible that a high temperature superconducting (HTS) Josephson tunnel junction radiates THz wave.

articleTitle: A high-resolution, wavelength-scanning, fast-data-acquisition THz-wave spectrometer for trace gases
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A compact, tabletop, high-resolution THz-wave spectrometer for trace gases was developed based on an injection-seeded THz-wave parametric generator. The chambers were purged with pure nitrogen gas to avoid strong absorption of THz-wave by water vapor. THz-wave spectra were measured over the wide frequency range of 0.8 to 2.4 THz with a resolution better than 100 MHz. Monitoring of sub-ppm H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O concentrations in real time was demonstrated.

articleTitle: The Identification of Illicit Drugs Using Terahertz Spectroscopy and Imaging
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The detection and identification of illicit drugs can be realized by THz spectra and imaging assisted by proper data processing. The component spatial pattern of each sample was obtained and separated from the others by introducing the component spatial pattern analysis. Meanwhile, nine different illicit drugs were identified successfully from their THz spectra by BP neural networks.

articleTitle: Electrooptical sampling of ultrashort THz pulses by fs-laser pulses at 530 nm and 1060 nm
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Electrooptical sampling (EOS) of ultrashort THz pulses with the help of fs-pulses at a wavelength of 1060 nm and (by second harmonic generation, SHG) of 530 nm is reported.

articleTitle: On the Bandwidth ofMMW Waveguide Circulators
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: New concepts such as internal & external band-widening methods and bandwidth improving ratio are presented. The bandwidth methods derived are employed to explain the attempts in the literatures and direct our development of MMW waveguide circulator.

articleTitle: Infrared Spectroscopy of Deep Impurities in Ge and ZnSe
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We observed Fano resonances of the continuums and the excited states of deep impurities with LO phonons in Ge:Te and ZnSe:Li.

articleTitle: GaP Raman Terahertz (GRT) Spectrometer using High Resolution Cr:forsterite Lasers
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We have developed high resolution GaP Raman THz (GRT) spectrometer using Cr:forsterite lasers with gratings. Line-width below 1.5 GHz and wide tunable frequency range (0.6 -6.2 THz) of the GRT enables to measure materials which have sharp absorption bands, such as gases or solid samples at low temperature with sufficient resolution.

articleTitle: Analysis Methods of Oil Contamination for Terahertz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) is used to investigate water and soot contaminations in oils, exhibiting different dilution modes. For synthetic polyglycol oils, the water is dissolved due to the polar behavior of the oil, whereas in non polar mineral oils the water-oil compound forms an emulsion. This behavior is modeled with an effective medium approximation (EMA) formalism. Small soot agglomerates are remaining in suspension when mineral oils are polluted with soot particles. In this case, the absorption spectrum is dominated by scattering effects. Due to the small particle size of the soot agglomerates compared to the THz wavelength, coherent scattering is the dominant process.

articleTitle: Tamm Problem And Terahertz Radiation In Nonlinear Optics
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We report on the remarkable similarities between the generation of terahertz(THz) radiation by nonlinear conversion in a slab and the radiation mechanism involving moving external charges, as discussed in the Tamm problem. The predictions of the theory are validated by experimental observations.

articleTitle: Formation Energy of Arsenic Impurities in MCT: First-Principles Study
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In our previous work, we have reported the relaxations, bonding mechanism and electronic structure of As<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Hg</sub> in Hg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sub>Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sub>Te and the effect of Hg vacancy defect on the properties of MCT. In order to give fully understanding of the solubility of As in-situ impurities in MCT and the concentration of the Hg vacancy, and especially give some hint of the compensation between the native defect and extrinsic dopant, we have performed the first principle total energy calculations to systematically investigate the formation energy of the arsenic in-situ impurity and the Hg vacancy defect of Hg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Te.

articleTitle: Transient Space-Charge Waves in Semi-insulating GaAs Photoconductor
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Transit space-charge waves effect in semi-insulating GaAs photoconductor are investigated by numerical simulation in this paper. The form process of space-charge waves is brought forth in the result of simulation.

articleTitle: Quasi-optical Material Measurements with Help of Diffractive Optics
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The monitoring of the composition of materials is an important problem of applied spectroscopy using optical, infrared, microwave and THz wavelength bands. MM and THz waves ensure better spatial resolution than microwaves and they can be used for material testing in media that are opaque for optical and infrared radiation. Whenever dielectric components are used in MM and THz wavebands, a precise knowledge of the dielectric properties of the material is essential. The developments original setups for dielectric material probing simultaneously at several discrete wavelengths within the same local zone are described.

articleTitle: Terahertz Spectroscopy of Furosemide
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Low frequency vibrational modes of furosemide were measured with terahertz time domain spectroscopy at room temperature. The different crystalline forms of furosemide were also measured. A clear difference between their spectra was observed. This makes the identification of polymorphs of furosemide easy and quick.

articleTitle: Multi-frequency Terahertz Generation in Aperiodic Optical Superlattices
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We investigate theoretically the generation of multi-frequency terahertz radiation in a LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> superlattice with an aperiodic structure. Such an aperiodic domain-inverted optical superlattice is designed in a quasi-phase-matching scheme. Second-order nonlinear optical rectification of femtosecond pulses gives rise to a terahertz waveform whose multi-frequency modes are determined by the aperiodic structure properties. The relationship between multi-frequency modes terahertz generation and aperiodic structure parameters is also analyzed and studied.

articleTitle: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy system using compact probe heads connected with large-mode-area photonic crystal fibers
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We constructed terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) systems using compact probe heads, which are connected with large-mode-area photonic crystal fibers (LMA PCFs), which in turn are used for guiding ultrashort optical pulses to THz probe heads. The LMA-PCF based THz-TDS system had comparable THz radiation power and bandwidth with those obtained by a conventional THz-TDS system with free-space optical arrangement. This is because LMA PCFs are suitable for high-power delivery without introducing non-linear effects.

articleTitle: Power Scaling of Widely-Tunable Monochromatic and Quasi-Single-Cycle THz Sources
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Our recent progress on the development of optically-pumped efficient THz sources from monochromatic waves to quasi-single cycles will be reviewed.

articleTitle: Superlattice Electronic Devices as High-Performance Millimeter- and Submillimeter-Wave Sources: Current Status
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: GaAs/AlAs superlattices were grown by molecular-beam epitaxy to study how thermal management and circuit parameters affect the performance of these structures when used as negative differential resistance devices. The fabrication process was adopted from that of GaAs tunnel injection transit-time diodes. The devices were evaluated between 60-270 GHz. RF power levels >70 mW with DC-to-RF conversion efficiencies >4% and >10 mW were measured at around 62 GHz and 130 GHz, respectively. These results demonstrate the potential of these devices as continuous-wave terahertz sources.

articleTitle: Theory of Vavilov-Cherenkov Radiation in a Hermitian Media
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Theoretical study and computer simulation on Vavilov-Cherenkov radiation (VCR) in a Hermitian media (HM) with and without absorption are given in the paper. Analytical solutions of the VCR in HM have been obtained, based on which the phase velocity and Cherenkov phase cone, the group velocity and Cherenkov group cone and the radiation power have been found. The fine inner structure of VCR is studied and discussed in details as well.

articleTitle: Magnetic Priming of a Relativistic Magnetron
