publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Magnetic priming [1] experiments performed on the UM/Titan relativistic magnetron (6-vane, -300kV, 5-10kA, 0.3-0.5 mus) have shown improvements in magnetron performance over baseline operation. In the current experimental setup, three, 4-cm long magnetic wires (Mu-Metal) are located within the cathode structure, centered beneath the emission region, and spaced 120 degrees apart. These wires produce magnetic perturbations with N/2 azimuthal-symmetry (for pi-mode in an N vane magnetron). Because of the close proximity of the priming structures to the cathode surface, the magnetic perturbations are strongest in the region where the electrons are emitted into the magnetron interaction space.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Cusp Gun for use in Gyro-amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Gyro-amplifiers require relativistic electron beams with low velocity spread and with a high fraction of the electron energy associated with the cyclotron motion. For harmonic operation and mode control an axis-encircling beam is desirable. The passage of an electron beam through a non-adiabatic magnetic field reversal (cusp) converts part of the electron beam's axial velocity into axis-encircling transverse velocity. This magnetic field is produced using two solenoids wound in opposite sense. The main cavity coil produces the field required for interaction whilst a smaller secondary coil, which is positioned just behind the cathode surface, produces a reverse field. A cusp-based electron beam forming system, yielding a 10 MW, 150 kV, 70 A axis-encircling beam for use in a gyro-TWA will be presented. The latest results from numerical simulations and experiments are presented and compared.

articleTitle: Room Temperature CW Operation of Antimonide MQW Laser Diodes beyond 3 μm
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Room temperature continuous wave operation of AlGaAsSb/GalnAsSb MQW diode lasers emitting beyond 3 μm were demonstrated. To increase the valence band offset of the quantum wells, AlGalnAsSb digital alloy was introduced as barriers in the active region. Pulsed mode operation at 3.25 μm up to 50°C has been achieved.

articleTitle: Coherent synchrotron radiation in storage rings as a broadband high power terahertz source
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Coherent synchrotron radiation (CSR) is a fascinating phenomenon recently observed in electron storage rings and shows promise as a broadband source of terahertz radiation with average powers at the kilowatt levels. The ring source of CSR also has several other unique characteristics such as high repetition rate, stability, synchronization with X-rays, and shaping of the electric field pulse. However, because of the properties of the radiation and the electron beams needed to produce it, there are a number of interesting features of the storage ring that can be optimized for CSR.

articleTitle: A U-band voltage-controlled Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: This paper presents design and test results for a U-band Gunn voltage-controlled oscillator. A planar varactor tuned up the frequency of the oscillator is bonded on the substrate named duroid5880 with 0.254 mm thickness in fin-line circuits. A novel structure is employed to solve the problem of a planar varactor and a encapsulated Gunn diode. Experimental results show that the frequency of the Oscillator is from 58.2 GHz to 59.2 GHz within 30 V tuning voltage and the power output of the oscillator is higher than 25 mW.

articleTitle: Uniform beam shaper and beam divider in millimeter wave band
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A kind of uniform beam shaper which is designed using binary diffractive element and for millimeter wave application is studied in this paper. This kind of beam shaper transforms the incident Gaussian beam into quasi-plane beam with uniform amplitude. Finite element method combined with c simulated annealing method is used to design this kind of beam shaper. A kind of quasi-optical beam divider is also studied in J this paper, and this beam divider is used to divide the quasi-plane beam into several beams carrying equal powers. Numerical results of the beam shapers and the beam divider at 94 GHz are presented.

articleTitle: Light Induced Recovery of Polymer Field Effect Transistors
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We have used differential terahertz spectroscopy to monitor performance degradation in state-of-the-art polymer field effect transistors (pFETs) based on poly[(9,9-dioctylfluorene-2,7-diyl)-co-(bithiophene)] (F8T2). After extended periods of operation holes are trapped in the polymer, increasing the device's threshold voltage. We monitor the trapped charge density using THz spectroscopy, and investigate the device's recovery as trapped holes are thermally removed. Illuminating the devices for a period with above-bandgap photons leads to a change in the terahertz transmission through the device, which is short lived after switching the light off.

articleTitle: Unexpected Infrared Absorption Spectrum of Magnesium Donor Impurities in Silicon
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The group-II magnesium, when diffused into silicon, is well-known to behave as an interstitial helium-like double donor. Previous study clearly indicates that the excitation spectrum of neutral magnesium donor has many features remarkably similar to those of group-V donors in silicon. Recently, however, from further study of the infrared absorption spectrum of magnesium donors, unexpected results quite different from a typical donor spectrum in silicon have been observed.

articleTitle: A Compact Electronically-Tuned Vector Measurement System For Submillimeter-Wave Imaging
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: An electronically tunable compact submillimeter wave transmission/reflection measurement system has been demonstrated at 560-635 GHz. The measured dynamic range is as high as 90 dB (60 dB across the entire frequency range), with less than 2deg of peak phase noise. The frequency agility of the system can be exploited to provide near real-time imaging capability using only a single pixel. This is accomplished by scanning the transmit and receive beams through the use of a frequency steerable lens placed at the transmitter and receiver.

articleTitle: Numerical Study of the Hamiltonian Gyrotron Map
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The recently derived Hamiltonian map for description of electron dynamics replaces the original continuous gyrotron differential equation by a discrete iterative map which runs much faster on computers than the small-step standard numerical integration methods, such as Runge-Kutta. It allows a significant reduction of the number of iteration steps required for acceptable accuracy. The gyrotron map is studied numerically for different combinations of gyrotron operating parameters.

articleTitle: MEMS Extended Tuning Range Varactor-Based True Time Delay Line Technology
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Novel RF-MEMS extended tuning range varactors are being developed for incorporation in arrays of RF MEMS based true time delay lines for use in millimeter-wave Phased Antenna Array (PAA) systems. A frequency of 28 GHz (Ka-Band) has been selected for the activity since it is a frequency region of considerable commercial, scientific, and military interest as well as being sufficiently high to result in small size units. The design of the 28 GHz proof-of-principle RF MEMS varactor based true time delay line is presented together with the fabrication process and the initial measurement results.

articleTitle: Manipulation on Infrared-Single-Photon by Frequency Upconversion
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The infrared-single-photon at 1.55 mum had been manipulated by the strong pump laser at 1.06 mum in the periodically poled lithium niobate crystal in the cavity of diode-pumped Nd:GdVO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sub> ring laser. A hour-level stable and 96% upconversion efficient technology had been developed.

articleTitle: Simulation of a 94GHz Second Harmonic Gyrotron Traveling Wave Tube Amplifier with Lossy Ceramic Interaction Region
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Simulation and design of a 94-GHz TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">82</sub> mode gyrotron traveling wave tube (gyro-TWT) amplifier operating at the second cyclotron harmonic are presented. The interaction circuit consisted of a new type of ceramic loading that provided the required loss for stable operation. Simulation results show that the amplifier can work stably with saturated peak power of 366 kW and a 3-dB bandwidth of 6.4%.

articleTitle: A Novel Zeroth-order Filter Based on CRLH Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A feature of the composite right/left-handed (CRLH) transmission line is the zeroth-order resonance. This property can be used to create a novel zeroth-order band-pass filter. Comparing with the traditional filter, the center frequency of the filter presented here is independent on the size of the filter, and the loss is relatively low. The experimental result of the filter are in good agreement with the simulation result.

articleTitle: Spin transport through a multimode quantum wire with Rashba spin orbit coupling under terahertz radiation
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We present results on ballistic transport in a quantum wire with strong Rashba spin-orbit coupling under terahertz radiation. Fano lineshapes can be found due the photon assisted interference. Mean while, the spin coherence at one propagating mode was reduced.

articleTitle: Terahertz Negative Differential Conductivities in Bulk GaAs
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Intrinsic dynamical conductivity spectra of GaAs have been determined from time-domain terahertz waveforms emitted from undoped bulk GaAs photoexcited by femtosecond laser pulses under strong bias electric fields. The cutoff frequency for the negative differential conductivities due to intervalley transfer gradually increases with increasing electric field and reaches ~800 GHz at 50 kV/cm. The temperature dependence of the cutoff frequency indicates that it is governed by the energy relaxation process of electrons from the L-to the Gamma-valley via successive optical phonon emission.

articleTitle: Plasmonic response in one- and two-dimensional periodic structures of metallic cylinders
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The frequency selective behavior of photonic and plasmonic crystals has attracted considerable attention over the past years. We have investigated two- and three-dimensional structures of metallic rods with a small distance compared to their diameter with a one-and two-dimensional periodicity. Under transverse magnetic (TM) incidence of terahertz (THz) radiation no transmission can be observed, while under transverse electric (TE) incidence the structures presented here show plasmonic behaviour, which leads to an effective plasma frequency. The effective plasma frequency for different rod diameters and geometries is determined with a simple model and compared to numerical simulations and experimental results.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional electron systems under microwave radiation
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The analysis of electronic transport phenomena in low-dimensional systems under microwave illumination led to the observation of unexpected new phenomena like the so-called microwave induced zero resistance state [Smet, JH., et al., 2005 ] or a new type of periodic voltage oscillations as a function of a magnetic field [Kukushkin, IV., et al., 2005] . The talk will present an overview about new developments in the field of electronic transport in low-dimensional systems with the focus on THz-spectroscopy and THz-detection.

articleTitle: Microlaser Pumped Narrow-linewidth Terahertz-Wave Parametric Generation
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We developed injection-seeded terahertz wave parametric generator pumped by microlaser. Microlaser is the half palm-sized, LD-pumped single-mode microchip Nd:YAG laser, delivers 1.1 MW peak power pulses (530 muJ/pulse) with 430 ps pulse width at 100 Hz repetition rate. This THz-wave source generated narrow-linewidth THz-wave by injection seeding for the idler-wave. We observed its peak output power of more than 20 mW (2 pJ/pulse) at 1.6 THz and its palm size, portable source offer good advantages for many applications.

articleTitle: Resonance Fluorescence of a Driven V-Type Three-Level Atom
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We investigate the resonance fluorescence spectrum of a three-level atom driven by two coherent laser fields in a V-type three levels with emphasis on the detuning effect. In the presence of the detuning of the first laser from exact resonance, there emerge some new structures in the resonance fluorescence spectrum. By applying the dressed-atom theory, we give an explanation for these interesting phenomena.

articleTitle: Analysis of Dielectric Loaded Complex Horn Gaussian Beam Launcher by Hybrid Technique of FEM and Gaussian Mode Expansion
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Summary form only given. High performance Gaussian beam launchers are required in quasi-optical power combing system for the transformation of power from active devices to free space fundamental Gaussian beam mode. The conical corrugated horn appears to be a popular choice (Olver, 1992) which can produce a nearly perfect Gaussian beam. Dielectric cone loaded horn antenna exhibit comparable performance at millimeter waves where the conventional corrugated horn is difficult to construct (Olver et al., 1998). A dielectric lens can be added to the central dielectric corn to obtain a constant phase front over the aperture, which will improve the aperture efficiency of the horn (Olver and Philips, 1993). Imposing a curved profile on the horn will give additional degree of freedom for obtaining better performance, which has successfully been applied in the design of corrugated and dielectric loaded horns (Philips and Olver, 1994). In most cavity-based solid state sources, rectangular waveguide outlets are often used. In this case, rectangular pyramidal launchers are easy to be connected. In this paper, the above stated techniques are applied on the rectangular pyramidal launchers for obtaining high transformation efficiency at D-band. An efficient hybrid technique of finite element method (FEM) and Gaussian mode expansion method has been proposed for the analyses of dielectric loaded complex horn Gaussian beam launchers. The formally exact Gaussian modes are used to express the free space fields. The finite element method is employed to analyze the launcher region. These two methods are combined through the boundary condition on the interface. A matrix equation for discretized electric fields in FEM region can then be deduced. The tangential electric fields on port surface of the launcher are obtained by solving this matrix equation. Then the main mode reflection coefficient can readily be calculated. Meanwhile, the solution to the electric fields on the output port surface can be used to determine the amplitude of each Gaussian mode, and further determine the transformation efficiency of the launcher.

articleTitle: Position-dependent Photoluminescence Across a PN junction Formed on P-type HgCdTe by Ion-milling Technique
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Photoluminescence spectroscopy was used to characterize a PN junction device formed on p-type mercury-cadmium-telluride (HgCdTe) material by ion-milling technique [1]. It was observed that the luminescence peak of the ion-eroded region shifted strongly to shorter wavelength.

articleTitle: Modulated Photoluminescence Spectra Study on Narrow-gap HgCdTe Liquid Phase Epitaxial Films
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Temperature- and excitation-dependent modulated photoluminescence measurements are performed on narrow-gap liquid phase epitaxy (LPE) Hg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Te (MCT). By combining with the second-order derivative and curve fitting, the band-acceptor transition is identified which is related to Hg vacancies. The energy level of this Hg vacancy locates at 12 meV (at 11 K) above the valence band.

articleTitle: Hot phonon effect in resonant-phonon-assisted terahertz quantum-cascade lasers
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We have studied the hot electron and phonon transport in resonant-phonon-assisted terahertz (THz) quantum-cascade lasers (QCLs) by using the semiclassical Monte Carlo method. The hot phonon effect is included in the Monte Carlo simulation by introducing a time constant accounting for the decay of polar optical phonons into other phonon modes. It is found that nonequilibrium polar optical phonons may modify the electron-phonon interaction, affect the electron distribution in different subbands, and consequently change the device current.

articleTitle: Direct Detection of THz Signals with an NbN Superconducting Tunnel Junction
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: NbN superconducting tunnel junctions (STJ) have a gap frequency reaching 1.4 THz, although demonstrating relatively large leakage current over Nb ones. In this paper the direct-detection performance of an NbN/AlN/NbN STJ is investigated at 0.5 THz with the aid of a Fourier transform spectrometer.

articleTitle: Heterodyne Mixing Performance of Distributed Nb Superconducting Junction Arrays at 1.2 THz
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In this paper we focus on the investigation of the heterodyne mixing performance of distributed Nb superconducting SIS junction arrays at 1.2 THz, which have individual SIS junctions uniformly distributed (connected in parallel) along a superconducting thin-film microstrip line.

articleTitle: Analysis of a Multilayer Slab Waveguide for Edge-Coupled THz Photomixer Applications
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A multilayer dielectric slab waveguide for the edge-coupled terahertz photomixer source applications is studied. The top layer of the dielectric waveguide structure is made of an ultra-fast photo-absorbing material, wherein the power of the guided modes are being absorbed and converted into a terahertz signal. The optical field and power distributions inside the waveguide structure are presented.

articleTitle: High Power Diode Pumped Vertical Externalcavity Surface-emitting Lasers (VECSELS)
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We describe the theoretical analysis and calculations of the 980 nm high-power diode-pumped vertical external cavity surface emitting laser (VECSEL). The VECSEL with active region of InGaAs/GaAsP/AlGaAs system can be operated near 500 mW in a single transverse mode.

articleTitle: A Novel Sub-Millimeter-Wave UWB Filter
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A novel sub-millimeter-wave bandpass filter used in ultra-wideband (UWB) systems is developed in this paper. The filter consists of two microstrip square ring resonators loaded with two lambda<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>/4 and 3lambda<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>/4 open stubs, respectively, where lambda<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> is the guided-wavelength at the midband frequency of the filter. The filter has a midband frequency of 25.5 GHz and a 3-dB bandwidth of 5 GHz (20%). Theoretical and measured results show that the filter is low loss within the passband, has sharp attenuations near the passband, and exhibits very wide stopband due to the introduced multiple transmission zeros.

articleTitle: Terahertz Radiation from Argon Gas Jet Excited with Intense Femtosecond Laser Pulses
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: THz wave radiated from Ar cluster target irradiated with intense femtosecond optical pulses is investigated. The results suggest that the strong THz radiation from the Ar cluster target originates from the efficient energy absorption of the optical pulses by the clusters.

articleTitle: Low-frequency modes of ionic liquids studied with terahertz-time domain spectroscopy and ab initio MO calculations
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We have obtained the dielectric spectra of ionic liquids with the terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) in a frequency range from 3.3 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> to 140 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. Ionic liquids composed of dialkylimidazolium or quaternary ammonium have been examined. The ionic liquids show broad but structured THz dielectric spectra, which could be assigned to the bands of inter-ion motions. The DFT calculations of respective cation-anion pairs give inter-ion vibrational modes in the THz region. The bending-like inter-ion motions, which originate from the rotational, translational, or torsional motions of the ions, are located below 100 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> whereas the inter-ion stretching motions are located above 100 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>.

articleTitle: Analysis of radome at millimeter wavelengths
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In this paper dielectric radome at millimeter wavelengths is analyzed by ray tracing and diffraction integral method. The ray tracing is used to calculate the equivalent electric and magnetic currents on the out surface of the radome, in computation the multi-reflection between interfaces of radome has been considered, and the equivalent currents is obtained by the superposition of multi-exit rays. The radiation pattern is calculated by diffraction integral method. Radiation pattern of the antenna with and without radome are presented.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Determination of Dielectric Permittivity and Magnetic Permeability of Bulk Samples by THz Time-Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We propose and demonstrate several methods for the simultaneous determination of complex permeability and permittivity of materials using THz time-domain spectroscopy.

articleTitle: The Study of Improving the Performance of HgCdTe Photovoltaic Detectors with Anti-reflection Coating
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Thls paper presents a method to improve HgCdTe detectors' performance by anti-reflection coating. Back-illuminated HgCdTe photovoltaic detectors have been fabricated on molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) HgCdTe layer on top of GaAs substrate by ion implantation doping. ZnS film is deposited on the surface of GaAs substrate by magnetron sputtering. With this AR coating, the black body detectivity, responsivity and quantum efficiency have the increase of 41%, 45% and 100% respectively. That is a great help to improve the property of HgCdTe detectors.

articleTitle: The effect of composition on non-stoichiometry ferroelectric Potassium Lithium Niobate Single Crystals
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The transmittance spectra showed that the crystal with higher Li content had better transmittance intensity.

articleTitle: Theoretical results of vertical external cavity surface emitting laser (VECSEL)
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We calculate the characteristic parameters of 980 nm infrared vertical external cavity surface emitting laser with the KP method and give the result of the relative longitudinal confinement factor, threshold gain and output power.

articleTitle: Infrared Optical Properties of Bi4-xNdxTi3O12 Thin Films Prepared by a Chemical Solution Method
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Infrared optical properties of Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4-x</sub>Nd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Ti<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub> [BNT(x=0,0.25,0.50,0.75)] thin films have been investigated using the infrared spectroscopic ellipsometry in the wavelength range of 2.5-11.4mum (0.11-0.50eV). Their refractive index decreased and extinction coefficient increased as the wavelength increased. Both the refractive index and the extinction coefficient decreased as the concentration of Nd increased. In addition, the wavelength and Nd concentration dependence of the absorption coefficient showed the similar behavior to that of the extinction coefficient.

articleTitle: Analytical theory of novel configurations of THz and sub-THz sources driven by linear electron beam
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Fundamentals of the theory of classical microwave sources driven by linear electron beams (klystrons, traveling-wave tubes, backward-wave oscillators) were developed long time ago. This theory was developed for devices with an axially symmetric interaction space. For operation in the THz and sub-THz frequency ranges, it is preferable to use planar microwave circuits because at short wavelengths fabrication of only such circuits is possible. This trend makes it necessary to generalize the fundamentals of the existing theory to the case of devices lacking the axial symmetry. Sheet-beam and some configurations of multiple-beam klystrons as well as orotrons and klinotrons can serve as examples of such devices. Present paper summarizes results obtained by the author in recent years. It includes: (a) formulation of the general theory, (b) analysis of mode selectivity in multiple-beam klystrons, (c) analysis of mode coupling effects in sheet-beam klystrons, (d) analysis of the monotron instability in sheet-beam klystrons, (e) analysis of effect of transverse nonuniformity of the RF field on efficiency of such devices, (f) linear and nonlinear theory of the orotron. It is believed that such a simple analytical theory can help designers to evaluate the optimal parameter space where it makes sense to perform a more accurate design of THz sources with the use of available 3D-codes.

articleTitle: Phase Effects In Terahertz Pulsed Imaging
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We have generated images of five tooth slices and three plastic step-wedges over a range of frequencies contained within a broadband terahertz pulse. It is observed that the boundaries between different types of materials (or thickness) are frequency dependent. A quantitative model of such image artefacts, involving the parameters of radiation frequency, sample thickness and material refractive indices, successfully reproduces the experimental data.

articleTitle: An Unconditional Stable Transient Analysis For Arbitrarily Shaped Structures Applying Hybrid Technique
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We present an unconditional stable time domain solution for three-dimensional arbitrarily shaped structures illuminated by a short pulse wave. A hybrid technique is applied to get stable transient data using early-time and low-frequency data. The time domain electric field integral equation formulation with a central differencing scheme is used to obtain the early time data, and stable late time data can be obtained by applying a hybrid method utilizing low-frequency data. The time domain solution method is based on marching-on-in-time technique and the hybrid method is based on the singular value decomposition for direct extrapolation of a causal signal.

articleTitle: Investigation of UTC and PIN Performance for THz Applications.
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The operation and performance of an InGaAs/InP uni-travelling-carrier photodiode (UTC-PD) has been studied using a commercial device simulator. We compare the UTC-PD with conventional PIN photodiodes, focussing particularly on evaluating the intrinsic device performance.

articleTitle: Laser Optimisation of Photoelectric Properties of Variable Bandgap CdHgTe layers for Multiband IR Detection
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The fabrication procedure of dual-band IR detectors has been developed by using laser activation of variable bandgap epitaxial Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Hg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Te layers at certain depths with the corresponding compositions x to increase the photosensitivity in the atmospheric window regions.

articleTitle: 128 Channels of Integrated Filter Array in the NIR Region Fabricated by Using The Combinatorial Deposition Technique
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A combinatorial deposition technique is developed to fabricate integrated narrow bandpass filters (NBPFs) on a single substrate. It is highly efficient for the fabrication of integrated filter arrays in optical regions. An array integrated with 128 NBPFs has been fabricated by using the technique with only a nine-step deposition process. The pass-bands of the filters distribute almost linearly in the range of 722.0-880.0 nm. Their relative bandwidth is smaller than 0.44%.

articleTitle: Resonant tunneling through single InAs quantum dot at room temperature
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Transport properties of freestanding InAs quantum dots on GaAs(001) are investigated by means of conductive atomic force microscopy. Resonant tunneling through the hole state of valence-band of single quantum dot is observed at room temperature. The threshold bias for resonant tunneling is related with the dot size, while the amplitude of tunneling current changes little when the height of dot varies from 2 to 10 nm.

articleTitle: Wave guide type photo receiver module with 20 dB amplifier at 60 GHz millimeter wave frequency band
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: 60 GHz Millimeter wave band photo receiver modules with wave guide type photo detector and InP HEMT preamplifier were developed. The photo-RF conversion gains of photo receiver modules in 60 GHz band were measured as about 20 dB.

articleTitle: Design of Curved EBG Structures and its Application on Cylindrical Conformal Microstrip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: According to the reflection condition of optics Bragg, two kinds of two-dimensional curved EBG structures are designed and their bandgap characteristics are observed, and they are applied to the cylindrical conformal microstrip antennas for the first time. The simulation results indicate that, the higher harmonics of the antenna with EBG are perfectly suppressed comparing with the normal cylindrical microstrip patch antenna without EBG.

articleTitle: 256×1 doped-InGaAs mesa infrared focal plane array
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We have made 256×l front-illuminated mesa doped-InGaAs infrared focal plane array (FPA) with two CTIA-structure L128 read out integrate circuit at two sides. The mean peak detectivity of the detectors is 1.33×1012 cmHz1/2W1 at 278K. The ununiformity of response is 19.3% at room temperature.

articleTitle: Integrated Design and Research of Ka-band Electronically Large Mono-pulse Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Thls paper presents a scheme of electrically large mono-pulse circularly polarized array, which works at Ka-band. A hybrid algorithm for electrically large array design is also studied. One kind of patch power divider of high power dividing ratio, which can be satisfied with array weighing method, is designed and calculated. The utilizing of planar sum/difference network in the design reduces the size of antenna effectively. The computation results achieve the desired performance of the antenna, which are also verified by experiment.

articleTitle: Study of THz Radiation Intensity Generating from GaAs Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We make out the time domain waveforms of THz radiation in both near field and far field generated by a GaAs dipole antenna by simulation based on the current surge model. The influences of current carrier lifetime and mobility on THz radiation intensity were discussed.

articleTitle: Intersubband Absorption in Coupled Double Quantum Wells Driven by a Strong Terahertz Field
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The quasienergy ladders of a symmetric double quantum well driven by a terahertz (THz) field are nonperturbatively calculated within the Floquet theory. The dependence of the quasienergies on the intensity of the driving THz field is discussed. Avoided crossings and crossings of the quasienergies belonging to same and different parity classes are demonstrated. The weights of the THz sidebands of the intersubband transitions are also presented. The weights of the n-th sideband are symmetric between the different sets of the transitions with n positive and negative respectively, while the weights of the n-th sideband are asymmetric between the same sets of the transitions with n positive and n.

articleTitle: Phase Shift in Far-Infrared/Terahertz Resonant Cavity Enhanced Mirrors
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The undoped/doped GaAs structures have shown successfully in the reflectivity of far-infrared (FIR)/terahertz (THz) resonant cavity enhanced (RCE) mirrors, but failed to yield matched phase shift, which has been obtained under resonance condition by sacrificing the reflectivity. Further increase of reflectivity may be realized by employing Au film on the bottom of the mirror.

articleTitle: High Resolution And Affordable HgCdTe IR Staring Arrays
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Staring array affordability has been the main goal of HgCdTe (Mercury Cadmium Telluride / MCT) infrared (IR) array developments for the last ten years. A lot of progresses have been made concerning the uniformity and the increase in wafer size, the readout circuit functions including Analog to Digital Conversion, the decrease in pixel pitch and the production capacity. Based on CEA-LETI/Sofradir HgCdTe growth process using Molecular Beam Epitaxy (MBE) on Germanium substrate, large HgCdTe wafer sizes were manufactured including an outstanding crystal quality (see fig 1).

articleTitle: My Spectroscopic Career
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The author, Xuechu Shen in Stuttgart and worked with Prof. L.Genzel where we developed double beam and optically Fourier transform spectroscopy, investigated the impurity vibration in crystalline and amorphous semiconductors, as well as vibration spectroscopy of bio-molecules by use of self-developed techniques. In Shanghai the author worked fortunately with many outstanding students where we developed many spectroscopic techniques.

articleTitle: Airborne Hyperspectral and Infrared Remote Sensing Technology and Application
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: These instructions give you basic guidelines for preparing papers for conference proceedings. In China , the techonology of spectral information , especially the IR spectral information are attractive in airborne remote sensing field. The main recent progresses of some typical airborne spectral remote sensing systems are introduced in this article .

articleTitle: Phase-locking of a two-mode THz quantum cascade laser
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We studied the phase locking and spectral linewidth of a 2.7 THz quantum cascade laser by mixing its two lateral lasing modes using a superconducting bolometer mixer.

articleTitle: Performance Studies of Novel Impregnated Barium-Tungsten Scandate Cathode on the Millimeter-Wave Tubes
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: With a view to the updated technical progresses and improvements of modern microwave tubes, millimeter-wave tubes especially, there are strong demands in cathode for the realization of higher current density, longer lifetime with decreased sublimation rates, and greater resistance to poisoning from the operating environment, etc. In response to these demands, the authors have developed and implemented the production of an impregnated barium-tungsten scandate cathode, which uses scandium, barium, calcium, aluminum carbonates as emission materials which are impregnated into the tungsten matrix substrate directly. The preparation process of the cathode is described, and its performance studies were also conducted.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Characterization of InGaAlAs/InP based Uni-Traveling-Carrier Photodiodes
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We have fabricated and characterized InGaAlAs/InP uni-traveling-carrier photodiodes intended for photo-mixing and data-corn applications. Bandwidths up to 60GHz were recorded with 8.5mum diameter devices for which a matched, integrated antenna-detector circuit has been designed.

articleTitle: Simplified Analysis of a Coherent THz Cherenkov Radiation Generator
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A model of one or more electron bunches passing through a partial filled dielectric rectangular waveguide is introduced. Analysis results show that with the help of appropriate parameters chosen for the waveguide, the frequencies of the coherent wakefield pulses generated by Cherenkov radiation with TM mode in dielectric could be located in terahertz band. These pulses following the electron bunches are emitted at high power. The 2-D problem of this model was theoretically analyzed and the waveguide was also simulated through FDTD-PIC method.

articleTitle: Rapid Thermal Annealing Effect On Valence-band Splitting Behavior in GaNxAs1-x/GaAs
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Our investigation is about rapid thermal annealing(RTA) effect on valence-band splitting(VBS) of GaNxAs1-x. The observed VBS between light- and heavy-hole induced by lattice strain in GaNxAs1-x epilayers is gradually weakened by the RTA process. This could be attributed to strain relax caused by nitrogen reorganization after RTA.

articleTitle: Terahertz Pulse Generation in Organic Crystal DAST from Various Short Pulse IR Lasers
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We report unique THz spectra obtained from DAST emitters via optical rectification with three different pump sources.

articleTitle: Enhanced THz Transmission and Polarization Conversion in Double-Layer Metal Hole Arrays
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The transmission and polarization change of double-layer metal hole arrays have been studied in the terahertz region using the time-domain spectroscopy. The transmission spectrum shows drastic and complicated dependence both on the spacing and lateral displacement of the two layers. The large polarization change is observed when the symmetry of the lateral configuration of the two layers is low and the spacing is less than the wavelength of the incident THz wave. These properties are attributed to the resonant excitation of the surface plasmon-polaritons (SPPs) and the coupling of the SPPs excited on the surfaces of the metal hole arrays.

articleTitle: Terahertz Radiation from YBa2Cu3O7-δ Thin Film Antenna on LaAlO3 Substrate
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We report on terahertz radiation emitted from YBa<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7-δ</sub> thin film antennas on LaAlO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> substrate. Our results show that their properties are very similar to antennas reported on MgO substrate.

articleTitle: Present Status, Application and Prospect of the ECRH System in Large Helical Device
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: There are several important roles for the electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) methods in helical-type plasma experimental devices. One is to produce high-temperature and high-density current-free plasmas. Another is additional heating of electrons and resulting ion heating through equipartition. Plasma temperature and current profile controls with highly localized heating become advanced techniques to improve plasma confinement and to suppress some MHD instabilities. ECRH is also an ultimate candidate of a steady-state plasma sustainment.

articleTitle: International Organizing Committee, IRMMW-THz
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Welcome to IRMMW-THz2006. The joint 31st International Conference on Infrared and Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Terahertz Electronics is going to be held from September 18th to 22nd 2006 in Shanghai, China. The conference site is in the Hotel Equatorial Shanghai, which located in the center of the city, neighboring with Jing-An ancient temple, an ancient Buddhist temple with a much longer history than the city Shanghai itself! The abstracts have covered all important topics of the fields, such as IR, MMW and THz sources, detectors & Receivers; devices, images & instruments for IR, THz and MMW; Gyro-oscillators and amplifiers; IR THz MMW spectroscopy, both in frequency and time domains; IR, THz and MMW application in Astronomy, atmosphere and environmental sciences, biology and medicine, physics and chemistry, public security and industry.

articleTitle: Author index
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The author index contains an entry for each author and coauthor included in the proceedings record.

articleTitle: Author information
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Provides instructions and guidelines to prospective authors who wish to submit manuscripts.

articleTitle: Energy scalable and high beam quality THz-wave parametric oscillator using surface emitted cavity configuration
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We describe a possibility of the output THz-wave scaling in surface emitted TPO by simply using a larger beam size along with higher pump energy. The output energy was as six times as higher than that of the conventional surface emitted TPO though the input energy and pump beam cross-section area each increased 2.9 times. The efficiency enhancement by increasing a pump beam size was also obtained. The beam quality factors (M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) of THz-wave were also measured to be 1.15 x 1.25.

articleTitle: THz GaAs/AlGaAs Quantum Well Detector
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We have designed and tested basic operation of a GaAs/AlGaAs quantum well photodetector in THz range of spectrum (3 THz, 100 mum). Responsivity of a few mA/W was measured, however achieving of the background-limited performance was not feasible because of high level of the dark current. Suitability of the device for practical applications will depend on further improvements of the design. We believe that better performance can be attained by optimizing the doping levels in the quantum wells. To evaluate suitability of the quantum well detectors for THz imaging, a small (up to 32 elements) prototype array will be tested.

articleTitle: Scattering and Radiation Characteristics of Step Discontinuity in Left-Handed Slab Waveguide Operating in Evanescent Surface Mode
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The radiation characteristics of a step discontinuity in left-handed (LH) slab waveguide operating in evanescent surface mode are analyzed. Our method transforms the radiation problem into a propagation problem so as to tremendously simplify the calculation procedure. The dispersion properties of the slab are examined, from which the left-hand property of the operating mode is testified. The relative scattered power and radiation pattern of the step are given for the first time, from which the backward radiation of the stepped LH guide is clearly demonstrated. The opposite frequency scanning characteristic of the step is illustrated, which makes the considered structure promising candidate for new type of planar antennas.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Imaging on the KSTAR Tokamak via Simultaneous ECET/MIR
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A millimeter wave plasma diagnostic instrument is being developed for the KSTAR tokamak to image electron density fluctuations via microwave imaging reflectometry (MIR), and electron temperature profiles and fluctuations via electron cyclotron emission imaging (ECEI). The 2-D active and passive MMW imaging systems will be capable of simultaneously imaging fluctuations over an extended portion of the KSTAR plasma. System details, including preliminary optical and electronics designs, FSS notch filter, and antenna prototypes, are presented along with a discussion of a number of implementation options which include plasma coverage, spatial resolution, channel numbers, IF and RF bandwidths.

articleTitle: Spin, Charge and Lattice Excitations Investigated by Photoconductivity Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We review our recent work based on infrared and microwave photoconductivity spectroscopy. The technique allows us to study the interplay between spin, charge, and lattice excitations in semiconductor and ferromagnetic microstructures.

articleTitle: Terahertz sensitivity of Pb1-xSnxTe:In
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In this paper, two possible ways of terahertz radiation detection are discussed. The direct detection is based on the ferroelectric properties of Pb<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>Sn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Te:In (LTTI) and its photosensitivity in the submillimeter spectral range. Indirect detection is possible due to uniquely low noise equivalent power (NEP) of LTTI detectors in lambda < 20 mum spectral range.

articleTitle: A New Calbration Method For Measuring Permittivity Of Biological Materials
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: This paper describes an approach to measure a material's complex permittivity using the transmission line method (TLM). The complex permittivity is derived from the measured reflection coefficient of a waveguide section that is partially filled with the material sample under test. To remove errors associated with imperfect waveguide flange mating, an in-situ calibration method is introduced. Initial measurement results in the W-band (from 75 to 110 GHz) show improved accuracy with the new calibration method as well as promise of scaling to higher frequencies.

articleTitle: Influence of Gouy Phase Shift on THz Time-Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In THz-TDS, THz radiations have to be transformed generally to be focused on the sample. However, the THz frequency spectrum and temporal waveforms may be changed by Gouy phase shift in the focus . The Gouy phase shift is the well known pi phase shift with respect to a plane wave as a focused electromagnetic beam propagates through its focus . As we know, most of researches in relation to the interaction between the focused light and media still consider the light beam in the vicinity of the focus as plane wave, and ignore the phase singularities which could lead to the superluminal velocities . Here, we study the influence of Gouy phase shift on the THz-TDS by means of numerical calculation and corresponding experiments.

articleTitle: Widely Tunable Terahertz-Wave Generation by Collinearly Phase-Matched Difference-Frequency Generation from GaP
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We propose a novel method to realize widely tunable terahertz-wave generation from GaP by collinearly phase-matched difference-frequency generation. Our method makes it possible to achieve a wavelength-tunable output without decreasing the output efficiency, which can be used for wavelength sweeping in spectroscopy.

articleTitle: A high speed digital phase-locked receiver for microwave and millimeter wave amplitude and phase measurements
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A high speed digital receiver has been developed for microwave and millimeter wave amplitude and phase measurements. The receiver architecture based on a built-in Nyquist rate digital phase-locked loop, is presented to reduce the accuracy degradation caused by frequency error, which makes the receiver fit for various microwave and millimeter wave superheterodyne front-end. The hardwire logic implementation of core algorithm enhances its highest measurement speed up to 350,000 points per second, which is near an order of magnitude higher than that of the current popular amplitude and phase receivers, and potential increase is prospective.

articleTitle: FPLAPW investigations of electronic properties of IIB0VI tellurides in the generalized gradient approximation
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The electronic properties of zinc-blend ZnTe, CdTe and HgTe are systematically investigated using the FLAPW approach. We find that the essential features of density of states, the influence of d electrons on the band structure, and electronic charge distributions are insensitive to the choice of exchange-correlation potential. Some calculated fundamental parameters show an agreement with experimental and theoretical results.

articleTitle: Measurement of Dielectric Tensor and Magnetic Resonance Frequency of Magnetically Hard Thin Plate Gyrotropic Material
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A gyrotropic magnetic model that accounts for the large demagnetization field is developed to fit transmittance interference patterns measured from 46 to 166 GHz. Uncertainties of in estimates of the dielectric constant and magnetic resonance frequency are typically less than 2%.

articleTitle: Comparisons of Complex Permittivity Measurements Using Free-Space and Waveguide Fabry-Perot Resonators at E/W-band Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Dielectric materials with the real relative permittivity ranging from 5 to 16 are studied thoroughly at 60-110 GHz using the free-space quasi-optical and waveguide Fabry-Perot interferometer measurement techniques. The optical n and k constants can be obtained accurately even though the undesired standing waves resulting from the imperfection interfaces in the measurement system cause strong spikes in the measured Fabry-Perot interference fringe pattern.

articleTitle: Cascading in THz Wave Generation by Optical Rectification
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Cascading effects were analyzed for the THz wave generation by optical rectification in an electro-optic crystal using intense femtosecond optical pulses. Coupled equations describing the propagation of the optical and THz fields were solved numerically. Cascaded difference frequency generation within the pump pulse spectrum was observed to leads to red shift of the pump light spectrum and almost linear growth of THz amplitude as a function of propagation distance. Conversion efficiency of THz waves higher than the Manley-Rowe limit, which corresponds to 100% quantum yield, was obtained in the simulation using a ZnTe crystal.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional imaging with plasmagenerated terahertz waves
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Terahertz (THz) waves generated through four-wave mixing in laser-induced air plasmas are an ideal source for imaging arbitrary locations. Under an amplified laser beam, ionized ambient air as a mixing medium provides broadband pulses with an unprecedented THz electric field strength among all the optically induced THz waves from nonlinear materials. We report the use of plasma-induced THz waves for 2D imaging for the first time, and compare it to other methods.

articleTitle: Dispersion of Terahertz Surface Plasmon Polaritons on Metal Wire Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Dispersive behavior of terahertz surface waves on metal wires is experimentally and theoretically studied. This behavior is different from that of surface plasmon polaritons on planar metal surfaces or on metal nanorods at optical frequencies.

articleTitle: Transmission Properties of ENG-MNG Structure Based On CRLH Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The epsilon-negative (ENG) and mu-negative (MNG) materials were fabricated using the composite right/left-handed transmission line (CRLH-TL). The ENG and MNG materials are opaque in electromagnetic wave region, but the (complete) transparency phenomenon will occur in the ENG-MNG pair under special conditions, the energy flux concentrate on the ENG-MNG interface. The S-parameters measurements exhibit agreement with the simulated results.

articleTitle: BWO-spectroscopy of Ortho and Para Water
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: It is an intriguing challenge for researchers to separate water into its spin isomeric modifications -paramagnetic ortho-water and nonmagnetic para-water. Accessibility of these new forms of water could stimulate the research in many branches of science. We report on the application to this problem of the terahertz BWO-based technique as a diagnostic method.

articleTitle: Transmission-Mode Scanning Probe Laser Terahertz Emission Microscope
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We developed a transmission-mode scanning probe laser terahertz emission microscope (sp-LTEM). Femtosecond (fs) optical pulses are delivered and focused on the sample by an optical fiber probe with a beam diameter of 5 mum. The transmission-mode sp-LTEM system is superior to the conventional reflection-mode sp-LTEM system in the viewpoint of the signal sensitivity because emitted THz waves can be detected without being disturbed by the scanning probe itself. The spatial resolution is experimentally estimated as ~2 mum with the gold line and space patterns on a low-temperature-grown gallium arsenide (LT-GaAs) substrate.

articleTitle: Contactiess Measurement of Conductivity of GaAs Wafers by Millimeter Waves
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A method to measure electrical conductivity of GaAs wafers by millimeter waves is presented. A compact equipment working at 94 GHz was used to measure the millimeter wave signal reflected from the wafer surface. A contactless measurement is realized and the measurement result is independent of the thickness of the wafer.

articleTitle: Dielectric Properties of Common Household Powders at Millimeter Wave and Terahertz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Thls paper presents the refractive index, absorption coefficient, complex permittivity (real and imaginary), and loss tangent of talc, flour, and pesticide from 200 to 1,300 GHz. A unique resonance peak was observed in talc at 1,150 GHz.

articleTitle: Geometric Correction of IR Imaging Spectral Image Based on IMU/GPS Navigation System
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: In this paper, a process of geometric correction for IR scanning images based on GPS/IMU position and orientation data is proposed, which includes GPS/IMU data preprocessing, geometric correction according to the collinear equation, and multi-strip mosaicing. The experiment results show that the presented method get an ideal effect.

articleTitle: Study terahertz ellipsometry setups for measuring metals and dielectrics using free electron laser light source
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The ellipsometers for terahertz spectral range with free electron laser light source was constructed. Different schemes were compared, describing the sensitivity with analyzing measurement error. Setups were numerically simulated and compared with experiments. Terahertz ellipsometry spectra's for water based liquids, and dielectrics (PMMA, teflon, silicon) were obtained. Some optical constants (thickness, absorption, refractive indexes) were calculated from measurements.

articleTitle: THz Spectral Database for Forensic Chemistry
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Terahertz spectra of several dozen drugs and poisons were measured, and the database was constructed. Search and retrieve of the spectral database was tried with some commercially available search programs. The identification ability of each algorithm was compared and verified for accurate retrieval of the material.

articleTitle: Researches on Millimeter Wave 3D Imaging at Novosibirsk, Russia
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Researches on millimeter wave 3D imaging in Novosibirsk are described. The researches mainly focus on the analysis and design of diffractive and quasi-optical components or various lenses of real time 3D imaging system.

articleTitle: New Shallow Donors in High-purity Si
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Two new hydrogenic shallow donors with binding energies of 38.32 and 40.09 meV are observed, in addition to phosphorus (P) and antimony (Sb) donors, in n-type high-purity silicon crystals by means of high-resolution photothermal ionization spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Ab Initio Molecular Modelling of THz Spectra
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Molecular modelling can be used to predict and confirm THz spectra, and to gain information that may be difficult or impossible to obtain experimentally. There are a variety of approaches, and consideration must be given to the likely sources of error in the molecular modelling of THz modes.

articleTitle: The Fabrication of THz Photonic Filters Using Ultraviolet Based SU8 Micromachining
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Here we report on the development of an ultraviolet (UV) based exposure technique for the fabrication of high aspect ratio metallic pillar arrays. These arrays act as photonic band gap based filters. Completed structures show a relative transmission of up to 97% in the main pass band centred at 1.25 THz.

articleTitle: Zero-Bias Spin Separation in Quantum Wells
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: We show that in gyrotropic semiconductor structures spin-dependent asymmetry of electron scattering induce a pure spin current which, in contrast to the spin Hall effect, does not require an electric current to flow. The effect is observed in GaAs/AlGaAs quantum wells at free-carrier absorption of terahertz radiation in a wide range of temperatures from liquid helium up to room temperature. The results agree with the phenomenological description based on the symmetry. Experimental and theoretical analysis evidences unumbiguously that the observed photocurrents are spin-dependent and related to the gyrotropy of the low-dimensional structures. Microscopic theory of this effect based on asymmetry of photoexcitation and relaxation processes is developed being in a good agreement with experimental data.

articleTitle: Coupled Cavity Waveguides of Photonic Crystal Consisting of Magnetized Ferrite Medium
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: An exact approach to analysis of two-dimensional coupled cavity waveguides consisting of magnetized ferrite medium has been described This method is based on lattice sums' matrices and a T-matrix of an isolated cylinder. The new formula has restrained the computing error caused by beta-matrix, has improved calculating precision, and has reduced computing costs.

articleTitle: The Study of Coaxial Gyrotron with Two Beams
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Results of the theoretical analysis and computer simulations for the coaxial gyrotron with two electron beams (CGTB) are given. It is shown that CGTB has a number of advantages, the output power can be doubled and the mode competition can be significantly improved, the CGTB can also operates simultaneously at two modes with different cyclotron harmonics.

articleTitle: Transition of Absolute instability from global to local modes in a gyrotron traveling-wave amplifier
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: This study systematically characterizes the local absolute instabilities and their transitional behavior. The axial modes were characterized from the perspective of beam-wave interaction, which share many characteristics with the global modes. The transition from global modes to local modes as the distributed loss increases was demonstrated. The electron transit angle in the copper section, which determines the feedback criterion, governs the survivability of an oscillation. In addition, the oscillation thresholds predicted using this model are more accurate than those obtained using a simplified model.

articleTitle: Design of A 3mm Second-Harmonic Complex Cavity Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Basing on the simulation of MIG, complex cavities and the self-consistent nonlinear analysis on interaction between electron-beam and wave of complex cavity gyrotron, the design of 3 mm second-harmonic complex cavity gyrotron operating on mode H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</sub>-H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">03</sub> are reported. Initial experiments show a peak power of 118 kW, an efficiency of 20.5%.

articleTitle: 3-D PIC Simulations of 0.3THz Reflex Klystrons
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Three-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations for 0.3THz reflex klystron performed by commercial code "MAGIC3D" show that a micro-fabricated reflex klystron can be a promising radiation source in the THz frequency region. Using 1 keV, 20 mA electron beam, over 100 mW power transfer from the kinetic energy of the electron beam to the electromagnetic energy in the resonant cavity could be obtained.

articleTitle: Submillimeter Wave ESR Measurement of a Finite Haldane Chain System Y2BaNi0.96Mg0.04O5
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The edge states in the finite S=1 Haldane chain are expected to have different energy structures depending on the chain length due to the interaction through the finite chain. Electron spin resonance (ESR) signals coming from the finite chains with various chain length have been observed separately in Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>BaNi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.96</sub>Mg<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.04</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sub>, which is a famous Haldane system doped with non-magnetic ions, due to the high spectral resolution of our submillimeter wave ESR. From the analysis, the information about the correlation length in the Haldane system at low temperature has been obtained directly by the experiment for the first time.

articleTitle: Effects of Self-Fields on Gain in a Helical Wiggler and Axial Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A theory for gain in a free-electron laser with helical wiggler and axial magnetic fields in the presence of the self-electric and self-magnetic fields is presented. It is shown that for group I orbits, gain decrement is obtained relative to the absence of self-fields while, for group II orbits, gain enhancement is obtained.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo Simulation of Terahertz Radiation Waveform from SI-GaAs Photoconductive Antennas
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: A self-consistent Monte Carlo approach is used to simulate the time resolved terahertz radiation from Si-GaAs photoconductive antenna. An adjustable energy and width of fs laser pulse is applied to illuminate Si-GaAs-based photoconductive antennas. The THz wave profile by simulation is similar to THz radiation waveform from experiment. We analyzed carrier dynamics in photoconductive antenna, and interpreted the mechanism that the width of emitted THz pulse was much wider than the pump pulse. And the mechanism that THz bipolar waveform emitted from Si-GaAs-based photoconductor trigged by high energy optical pulse at lower biased voltage was studied.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave 0- π phase modulation transceiver module
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: This paper presents a millimeter-wave miniature 0- π phase modulation transceiver modules fabricated with a complete MMIC chip set. The transmitter and the receiver module share a X-band DRO. The transmitter module, which consists of a quadruple multiplier, a 0- π phase shifter, a switch and power amplifier, exhibits 28 dBm output power, 25 dBc carrier wave suppression and 28 dB on-off radio. With the receiver module, which consists of low noise amplifier, a mixer, a quadruple multiplier and a medium power amplifier, 6 dB single-side band noise figure with 10 dB down-conversion gain has been achieved.

articleTitle: Transmission Property of Dielectric Phase Gratings with Stepped and Curved Profiles
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: Grooved dielectric phase gratings are commonly used for transferring millimeter or submillimeter wave power generated by an array of active sources into a pseudo-plane wave which is further reconstructed as a main Gaussian beam to fulfill power combination. Modified grooved dielectric gratings with multi-step or curved profiles have more degrees of freedom for adjusting the phase of exciting Gaussian beams to form a pseudo-plane wave. In this paper, the transmission property of the modified dielectric gratings is analyzed by a hybrid technique of finite element method (FEM) and Gaussian mode expansion method. The transmitted field through the modified dielectric gratings is calculated. Numerical results of transmission coefficients are presented for the gratings with different profiles at D-band.

articleTitle: Multi-target Detection in FMCW Radar based on Six-Port Technology
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The traditional FMCW radar has its own limitation in multi-target detection. Six-port radar is proposed as a new way to solve this problem because of the phase measurement capability. The method of using six-port radar to suppress false alarm is discussed and computer simulations prove that the method is valid and practical.

articleTitle: Substance Detection for Security Screening Using Terahertz Imaging Technology
publicationTitle: 2006 Joint 31st International Conference on Infrared Millimeter Waves and 14th International Conference on Teraherz Electronics
abstract: The ability of terahertz radiation to render many non-metallic and non-polar substances transparent provides for many security applications. In this paper we will focus on the possible application of terahertz radiation scanning the contents for illicit substances in common use suitcases in secure areas. Suitcases and contents were simulated by sandwiching a cotton sheet between nylon or plastic, with the cotton being laced with illicit substances of varying concentrations.
